## For your review

Non-blocking. Each entry says what was built or decided, what you'd notice in the game, and how
to change it. To change anything, write it in `studio/inbox.md`, for example "use formations
instead of clusters" or "make giving up take 2 seconds".

### Giants are drawn as wide as the room they take: they stand apart now, and a Warrior reads as a tall pillar (view track, M7-V3c, 2026-11-12-0546, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** Last session's pictures showed Teblor giants drawn inside each other, because their size was counted twice in their width. Now every unit's body is drawn exactly as wide as the room the rules give it, and the drawing scale only makes it taller. One place in the code changed; the selection ring, the red target ring, the corpse mark and the "cannot cast" mark all follow it. A new screen test plays the real Teblor from the shipped files (not a pretend faction) and checks all of this on every unit in the game.

**What you will see in the game.** Pictures in `studio/review/2026-11-12-0546/`, the same views as last session's in `studio/review/2026-11-11-2256/`. (1) **A Teblor base at the start** (`teblor-2-base.png`): five Gatherers stand in a row behind the Longhouse with a gap between each; last time they were one lumpy wall. (2) **A Warrior beside a Malazan Heavy Infantry** (`teblor-3-warrior-beside-soldier.png`): the giant is a pillar 1.5 m across and 3.75 m tall, the soldier 0.8 m by 1.8 m, so the giant is about twice the soldier each way and clearly taller than wide; last time it was a fat blob three soldiers wide. (3) **Giants in a group** (`teblor-4-crowding.png`): select three Warriors and five Gatherers and send them to one spot: eight upright bodies, each with its own green ring and health bar, touching only where the rules themselves let a crowd squeeze. (4) `teblor-1-setup.png` (the setup row, unchanged) and `teblor-5-war-dog-queue.png` (the Stables & Kennels queue reads "W×3" for a pack of three War-dogs). Malazan and Whirlwind units are unchanged to the pixel (one fixed-camera battle picture is byte-for-byte the same before and after). Clicking a giant works at its drawn edge: a click 3 pixels inside selects it, 3 pixels outside does not.

**The white flash I mentioned last time is not a bug.** A unit that is already hurt the first time it appears on screen flashes white for one frame: that is the normal "just got hit" flash. In a normal Teblor start it never happens (145 unit drawings checked, none white).

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) The look itself, decided at this session's plan: width from the room, `scale` for the height. Write **"giants: keep them wide"** in the inbox for the alternative (wide bodies, less room in the rules, every Teblor measurement redone). (2) **One of the game's own screen tests is red on purpose for one session.** QA found that a made-up unit that is both very wide and very short (nothing in the game is) gets a body narrower than its ring, and added a test that fails until that is fixed (BUG-1290). I let the giants' fix land now rather than hold it a session for a case no real unit reaches; the fix is the first thing the view track does next session.

**Rough edges.** BUG-1290 (S3) as above, next session. A crowd of giants squeezes a little closer than shoulder to shoulder in the rules themselves (8 of 28 pairs at 1.27-1.45 m where 1.5 m is touching); the screen shows exactly that, no more. The Teblor buildings are still drawn at normal size; the 1.25× the Teblor page asks for comes with the data's next landing.

**How to change it.** An inbox note about how giants should look. Sizes: `radius` (room, and now width) and `scale` (height) per unit in `game/data/factions/teblor/units.json`.

### The Teblor AI's slow start was measured 25 ways: reordering its build list is not enough, so nothing changed yet; a question about its first raid (data track, D29, 2026-11-12-0546, ACCEPTED, 1 fix round)

**What was done.** A computer-controlled Teblor player on Normal is slow: at ten minutes it is usually still in Age I and half the time it has not attacked (BUG-1241). This session measured, without changing the game, how far its build list alone can fix that: 25 different openings, each played in 40 AI-against-AI matches (four maps, against Malazan and Whirlwind, five seeds) for 15 game minutes. **No data file in the game changed, so there is no table of changed numbers this time.**

**What you would see in the game today.** Nothing new: the Teblor AI plays exactly as it did yesterday.

**What the measurement says.** The target was "Age II reached and a first attack sent by 10:00 in at least 6 of 8 matches".

| Opening | Seeds that meet the target | Age II by 10:00 (of 40) | Attacked by 10:00 | Took a second base | Built every building | Defeated by 15:00 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Today's ("War band") | 0 of 5 | 7 | 15 | 4 | 3 | 17 |
| A: Age II earlier, the same four-Warrior raid (V24) | 1 of 5 | 21 | 34 | 3 | 0 | 5 |
| A2: the same with a slightly smaller raid (V25) | 1 of 5 | 21 | 34 | 0 | 4 | 5 |
| B: Age II earlier, a two-Warrior raid (V14) | 4 of 5 | 28 | 40 | 1 | 4 | 18 |

So there is a real trade: a Teblor AI that raids early with two Warriors gets going fast and is beaten as often as today's; one that waits for four Warriors is beaten far less often (5 matches of 40 instead of 17) and reaches Age II three times as often as today, but still misses the ten-minute target. Every opening, today's included, loses most of its army between minutes 10 and 15.

**The first attempt was wrong and QA caught it.** The developer first handed over opening B's cousin on a ten-minute count alone; QA played it to 15 minutes and showed it never expands and loses more (BUG-1300), so the work was redone to the 15-minute horizon above. That is the fix round.

**Producer decision (owner may revisit).** **Nothing lands yet, and my provisional pick is the four-Warrior family (A or A2)**: an opponent that survives to field its Age II units is a better opponent than one that feeds you pairs of Warriors. The measurement also found the missing rule: the AI spends on army whenever it can, so the gold for Age II never piles up. A stand-in test of "save for the next building once the army is half a raid" met the target on 3 of 5 seeds with only 6 defeats and many more buildings. The sim track builds that as a per-opening setting next session (Request 52); then the opening, the Frenzy numbers and the buildings' size land together in one go (old saves refuse once, not twice). **Your call if you want it:** write **"teblor ai: early raid"** in the inbox for B instead.

**The player-facing text that would change when it lands** (the opening's description, shown where AI openings are listed): "War Lodge and Javelin Ground first, then Age II; four Warriors raid at 8 army pop, with Javelin Throwers beside them."

**Rough edges.** BUG-1241 stays open until the landing. Five seeds are fewer independent samples than they sound (two pairs of seeds often play out identically on the hand-made maps). BUG-1302 (S4): a line in the developer's summary put A2 in the wrong group; the table above is the corrected one.

**How to change it.** The opening is `game/data/factions/teblor/ai.json` (`standard`); the candidate is kept as a test file, `sim/Rts.Sim.Tests/Content/Fixtures/teblor_standard_d29.json`. An inbox note decides A, A2 or B.

### The rules for Blood-oil Frenzy's extra damage and its slow afterwards are built; you will see them when the Teblor numbers land (sim track, M7-4, 2026-11-12-0546, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** The Teblor page says a Shaman's Blood-oil Frenzy makes nearby warriors attack 40% faster **and hit 20% harder** for 10 seconds, **then leaves them Slowed 20% for 4 seconds**, and that the Blood-oil Anointing upgrade makes the Frenzy last 4 seconds longer; it also says Teblor buildings are drawn a quarter larger. Until now the data files could only say the "40% faster" part. This session added four general rules any faction's files can use: a status that adds damage to its bearer's own attacks, a status that leaves another status behind when it runs out, an upgrade that lengthens named statuses, and a drawing size for buildings.

**What you will see in the game.** **Nothing yet.** No shipped file uses the new rules; a Frenzy in today's build is still only the attack-speed part. When the data track lands the Teblor rows (the session after next): cast Frenzy on a group of Warriors and each blow on a Heavy Infantry does 26 before armor instead of 22; ten seconds later they all slow down for four seconds (a good moment for the enemy to run or strike); with the Anointing researched the Frenzy lasts 14 seconds. Your saves and recordings keep loading until that landing.

**Details worth knowing.** A javelin already in the air when the Frenzy ends lands without the extra damage (the bonus is read when the hit lands, like weapon upgrades). The slow does not happen if the unit dies, or if the Frenzy is re-cast before it ends (it is simply extended); re-casting during the slow gives the Frenzy back while the slow runs out. The Zealot's own frenzy is untouched.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) The new fields count toward the "is this the same game data" check only when a file uses them, so today's saves were not refused a second time this week; the tidier alternative (always counted) costs one more refusal. (2) The upgrade lengthens every timed use of the statuses it names by its owner (spells, zones, bites), not only the one spell.

**Rough edges.** BUG-1280 (S3): the sim's own tests add a pretend Frenzy row under the very name the real one will have, and 84 of them fail the moment the real row ships; fixed first thing next session, before the data lands. BUG-1281 (S4): two small wording / tidiness items. When a Teblor's after-Frenzy slow lands on a unit already slowed more strongly by an enemy for a shorter time, the strong slow is stretched to the full 4 seconds: the general stacking rule, noted for the balance pass.

**How to change it.** The numbers will live in `game/data/common/statuses.json` (the Frenzy row: damage, the slow, its length) and `game/data/factions/teblor/techs.json` (the +4 s); an inbox note changes any of them.

### The checks the real Teblor tripped are fixed, and a crowd of giants was measured: it arrives less tidily than a crowd of soldiers (sim track, M7-5, 2026-11-11-2256, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** Only checks and two sentences of documentation; no game rule changed. The 28 automatic checks that failed with the Teblor files (and two more that a Whirlwind-like faction would trip) now say what they mean: "the two original factions have no bite effect / no pack / no drawn scale", instead of "no shipped unit has one". No recorded result was changed to make anything pass, and QA proved the fixed checks still catch real faults (it switched off the dog's slow, weakened it, and made a pack of three spawn two: 14, 4 and 9 checks failed).

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing directly. Two facts worth knowing: (1) **Memory.** The game keeps some tables per body size. The giants' 0.75 m is a fourth size, which costs 131 KB more on the largest map (232.6 MB against 232.5). The check now allows exactly that per new body size and still catches a 100 KB leak. (2) **Crowds of giants.** Send 500 units to four nearby points, or 128 units to 64 spots, on 40 maps each. With 0.4 m soldiers about 288 of 500 end up standing at their point and the rest stop nearby when it is full; the same units widened to 0.75 m: about 173. Nobody is left walking forever in either case. In play: a big Teblor group ordered to one spot spreads over a wider area than a Malazan group and stops sooner, which is what bigger bodies do, but it is a number to watch in the balance pass.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The memory allowance is per body size, from the data**, rather than raising the limit by hand each time a faction adds a size. (b) **The giant-crowd figures are a report, not a pass / fail line** yet: I want the balance pass to say what "good enough" is for giants before a limit is set.

**Rough edges.** None open from this task. BUG-1220 / 1221 (two hand-tampering corners from last session) still wait for the sim's next clean-up.

**How to change it.** Nothing to tune; an inbox note if you want giants to pack tighter or looser (that is `radius` in the Teblor `units.json`).

### The game's own checks are ready for a third faction, a tampered save is refused, and the "units killed" count was right all along (sim track, M7-H1, the sim's clean-up, 2026-11-11-1317, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** A rehearsal at the start of this session (a copy of the Malazan added as a pretend third faction) showed 66 automatic checks failing just because a third faction existed. They are fixed, without changing a single recorded result: checks about "the two shipped factions" now say so, and checks that need "some unit" pick one in a way that does not depend on how many factions there are. A small tool now makes that pretend faction in one command, for future rehearsals. Three smaller clean-ups came with it (below).

**What you will see or feel.** In play, nothing. Three things at the edges: (1) **A save file edited by hand** so that a unit "was last hit in the future", or whose healing bookkeeping disagrees with itself, is refused ("can't be loaded") instead of loading into a subtly wrong match. QA threw 10,000 damaged saves at it: none crashed, none loaded wrong; 50 honest saves all load exactly. (2) **A typo in a healing rate** in the data (say 0.07 HP a second) now stops the game at start with a message naming the value and the step (0.05), instead of being silently rounded. The Teblor's 1 HP a second is fine. (3) **"Units killed" on the stats screen:** a test expected 72 where the game showed 68. The game was right. Four of an AI's own soldiers died to its own Cussers and mage fire, and killing your own men is a loss, not a kill (your rule since the team work in M6). The test was wrong and is fixed.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **Refuse an off-step healing rate** rather than round it: the same number written in two places could round two different ways. (b) **The "slow PC" question is closed.** The same code ran the speed tests red at 18:45 (about five times slower on one of them) and fully green at 21:31, both with nothing else running. It is the machine's own slow state, not the code; I stop measuring it unless a speed test fails while the PC is at its normal speed.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1222 (S3; fixed in session 2256, the entry "The checks the real Teblor tripped are fixed" above):** the rehearsal used a Malazan copy, and the Malazan have no bite effect, pack or drawn scale, so 28 checks that only the real Teblor trip were missed. That is why the Teblor are held one session (the entry above); it is the sim's next task, and rehearsals now use a copy that exercises what the new content uses (new rule 55). **BUG-1220, BUG-1221 (S4):** two more hand-tampering corners (an emptied unit slot that still carries a status; a wrong-case folder listed twice gets a misleading message), for the sim's next clean-up. Not done for time: three internal name clean-ups (BUG-1161).

### A healing unit says "Regenerating", the game is proven with three factions on the setup screen, in a match, in a save and in a recording, and "1 second" reads right (view track, M7-V3a, 2026-11-11-1317, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** Everything the screens must do for a third faction, proven on a pretend one ("Forged Third Host", a renamed Malazan copy made inside the test) because the real Teblor were being written at the same time. And the cue for the Teblor's faction bonus.

**What you will see or feel.** Today, in the shipped game, nothing new: no shipped faction heals by itself until the Teblor land. Then: **select one hurt Teblor and leave it alone. Six seconds after its last hit the word "Regenerating" appears in green under its state ("Idle"), and its hit points tick up; it disappears the moment the unit is hit again or reaches full health.** It shows for a single selected unit, not in the grid of thirty. With three factions the skirmish setup's faction list shows three names in the data's order, a newly added player defaults to the next faction, a match with one seat per faction starts, saves, loads and replays, the third faction's hall, worker, build menu and tooltips read its own names, and the stats screen lists it. QA looked at the screenshots of the setup, the match and the stats screen, and also pushed eight factions (the maximum; a ninth is refused with a clear message). The difficulty tooltips read exactly as before ("Thinks every 2 seconds", "thinks every 0.5 seconds"); if you ever tune an AI to think exactly once a second it now reads "1 second", not "1 seconds".

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The cue is one word from the text file** (`hud.regenerating`), shown only when the unit will actually gain health on the next tick, so it never lies; the alternative was a small icon, which waits for the art pass. (b) **Singular and plural are two text entries** ("{0} second", "{0} seconds"), so the tooltip sentences keep their words.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1231 (S3; fixed in session 2256):** three of the screen tests (two of them new this session) failed once the real Teblor were added, because they counted on exactly two shipped factions. **BUG-1230 (S3):** a faction name longer than about 25 characters stretches the setup's faction lists and pushes the Team column, and two columns of the stats screen, off a small window. No shipped or planned name is that long ("Malazan Empire", "The Whirlwind", "Teblor"); the view's next clean-up clips long names. The cue for a healing *spell* (rather than the faction bonus) is tested without a screen only, because no shipped spell grants healing yet.

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/ui.json`: `hud.regenerating` (the word), `setup.seconds_one` / `setup.seconds_other`; or an inbox note ("show Regenerating in the grid too", "use an icon").

### The last step before the Teblor: techs and spells are numbered by faction too, and every save and recording made before today refuses to load, once (sim track, M7-3b, 2026-11-11-0739, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** Inside the game every upgrade ("tech") and every spell has a number, and until now those numbers came from one alphabetical list across all factions. The Teblor's spell "Blood-oil Frenzy" sorts before the Malazan "Cusser", so adding it would have shifted every shipped spell's number, and with it every test fingerprint and recording. Now the numbers follow the same order file as the factions and units (last session): the shared upgrades first, then each faction's own upgrades and spells in the order the factions are listed. A new faction appended to the list moves no existing number (proven with a full Teblor stand-in carrying "Blood-oil Frenzy" and its upgrade). The data loader also looks names up through a small sorted index now, which undid last session's slowdown on a huge test file (ten thousand unit rows: about 1.2 s back to 0.3-0.4 s).

**What you will see or feel.** One thing, once: **a save or a recording made before today no longer loads.** Main menu → Load Game answers an old row with "This save was made with different game data and can't be loaded." instead of loading it; Watch on an old recording refuses the same way. It cannot be converted (an old save stores the old numbers); start a new match and save again, and that save loads normally. Nothing else changed: the same match plays out the same way. QA replayed 20 pinned scenes and all 42 Hard-against-Normal AI matches on yesterday's build and on today's and compared them line for line: every winner and every end time is identical (Hard still wins 32, loses 8, 2 undecided).

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **Renumber once, now**, while nobody has saves that matter, rather than give the Teblor's spell an awkward name that happens to sort last. The alternative kept old saves loading but left a trap for every later faction (the Tiste Andii's upgrades would have hit it in M9). (b) **Shared upgrades come first** so their numbers never move whatever a faction is called. (c) **No conversion of old saves**: a converter would be code used once, for saves from test play.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1190 (S4):** one old test recording still names an upgrade by its old number (the test passes only because that click was refused in both versions), and one test loop stops two upgrades short of the end. Both are test tidiness, fixed in the sim's clean-up next session. **The speed tests:** on an idle PC this morning they ran about twice as slow as when they were recorded, on yesterday's build as much as on today's (item 8 under Wanted), so they still cannot be judged (BUG-1170).

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/factions.json` (append a faction; never reorder: reordering renumbers everything and refuses every save again), or an inbox note.

### Arrows and bolts are drawn from exactly who fired at exactly whom, tooltips have no blank lines left, and the difficulty tooltips read the AI's thinking speed from the data (view track, M7-VH1, the view's clean-up, 2026-11-11-0739, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** (1) Last session the screen guessed who had fired each arrow by looking for the nearest unit at the launch point; 3 shots in 1,411 were guessed wrong (a shooter killed the instant it fired). The simulation now offers the screen a small read-only window ("who fired this shot, at whom"), and the guessing is gone: 0 wrong of 1,411 shots in the test brawl, plus 2,168 more over four other battles, and reading it never changes the match (checked tick by tick against a twin match nobody looked at). (2) The tooltip wrapping could leave an empty line in the middle of a tooltip when the text had a double space or a space next to a line break; it no longer can (0 blank lines in 50,000 random texts, and all 34 shipped descriptions come out word for word as before). (3) The Easy and Hard tooltips in the skirmish setup used to have "every 2 seconds" and "every half second" typed into the text; now the number comes from each difficulty's `thinkInterval` in the AI file, so a tuning change can't leave the tooltip lying.

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish setup → hover **Hard** in an AI slot's difficulty list: it now reads "Fair play with tighter decisions: **thinks every 0.5 seconds**, focuses fire, ..." (was "every half second"). Easy reads "Thinks every 2 seconds, ..." exactly as before. In a battle nothing looks different today (every shipped unit is size 1); when the giants arrive, a javelin leaves from the thrower's chest and lands at the victim's, every time.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **"0.5 seconds" instead of "half second"**: a number read from the data can't be a word; the alternative was keeping the nicer wording typed by hand, which goes stale when the number is tuned. Say "half second" in the inbox and the Hard tip goes back to typed words, with a test that fails when the data changes. (b) **The tooltip shows the interval the AI really keeps**: the game runs in 20 steps a second, so a setting of 0.333 s is really 0.35 s and the tooltip says 0.35. (c) **At a line break the wrap drops the spaces beside it** (my ruling on BUG-1126), so a line never starts or ends with a stray space.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1200 (S4):** if someone sets Easy or Hard to exactly 1 second, the tooltip would read "every 1 seconds" (no shipped value does; Normal is 1 s but its tooltip doesn't state it), and one stale comment in the code; the view's next clean-up. Four old view bugs I had listed for this session (BUG-0860 / 0830 / 0890 / 0861) turned out to be fixed since October: my bug index listed each twice, once as open by mistake. Cleaned up.

**How to change it.** The sentences: `game/data/common/ui.json`, `setup.difficulty_easy_tip` / `difficulty_hard_tip` (`{1}` is the seconds, `{0}` Hard's gather bonus in percent). The numbers: `thinkInterval` under `difficulties` in each faction's `ai.json`. Or an inbox note.

### The game can take a third faction now: the Teblor will land as data files without disturbing anything, and the AI prices a dog pack fairly (sim track, M7-3, 2026-11-10-1236, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** (1) **An order file for factions.** Until now the game numbered factions and their units by alphabetical folder name, so adding a `teblor` folder (which sorts between `malazan` and `whirlwind`) would have shifted every Whirlwind number and with it every test fingerprint, every saved recording and the master recording the tests compare against. Now a small file, `game/data/common/factions.json`, lists the factions in order (`malazan`, `whirlwind`) and a new faction is added at the end; unit and building numbers follow that order too. The two shipped factions' numbers are bit for bit what they were, the master recording did not move, and a test copy with a full Teblor folder appended plays a Teblor AI for five minutes (as an AI seat in a three-way and a duel) while every Malazan-against-Whirlwind fingerprint stays identical. (2) **A dog's price.** A War-dog pack costs 120 gold for three dogs; the AI and the end-of-match army-value graph now count each dog at 40 (its share), where before they counted each dog at the whole pack's price and the AI's queue counted a pack as one unit. (3) **A pack that could never fit the population cap is refused when the data loads** instead of sitting paid and stuck at the head of a queue for ever. Nothing in the shipped game plays differently (no shipped faction has a pack).

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing today. When the Teblor land: three factions in the skirmish setup's list, and a Teblor AI that attacks when its army is worth what its opening asks, dogs counted at 40 gold each. The end-of-match graph of a Teblor player's army value will read the sum of what the units are worth, not three times a pack.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **One order file in `common/`** rather than an "order" number inside each faction's own file (one decision in one place; a gap or a tie can't happen). (b) **A dog's worth is the pack's price divided by three, remainder dropped**: a 54-gold / 20-wood pack of three counts 18 / 6 a unit, 72 of the 74 paid; the war-dog's 120 / 0 divides exactly. (c) **Techs and spells are not under the order yet** (BUG-1171): their numbers are still one alphabetical list each, and a Teblor spell named naturally ("blood_oil_frenzy") would shift the Malazan and Whirlwind spells. I chose to finish the rule in the sim's next task with **one deliberate re-recording of the master recording and every fingerprint**, rather than force every future faction to pick names that sort after the shipped ones (which already fails for the Andii). **The cost to you: every recording you make before the next sim session will refuse to play after it, one more time; saves keep loading.** The Teblor roster waits one session for it so it can land whole.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1172 (S3):** loading the data got slower in a test with ten thousand unit rows (0.6 s → 1.4 s; the real game has 14 units and loads in a blink); fixed as a rider of the next sim task. **BUG-1173 (S4):** a pack cheaper than its count in a resource counts 0 of it for the AI (undocumented; no shipped pack does), a wrongly capitalised faction folder on Windows gets a confusing message, ten test files still name the two factions by hand. **BUG-1170 (S3):** the four speed-gate tests still fail on this PC at the base too, and QA found your own apps at 31-52 % CPU during the run, so they still can't be judged (item 7 under Wanted). **Update 2026-11-11-0739: BUG-1172 is fixed** (the load is faster than before M7-3: 0.3-0.4 s for ten thousand rows), **and BUG-1171 is fixed** (techs and spells are under the order file too: the first entry above). BUG-1173 and BUG-1170 stand.

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/factions.json` (append a faction's folder name; never reorder), or an inbox note ("dogs count the whole pack", "refuse nothing at load").

Pale Hills seed 2 with Hard in the second seat is now a Normal win at 57 minutes (one match lost there, four gained on Vathar). docs/03's old "25%" sentences are dated, not deleted (BUG-1184, fixed).

**How to change it.** `game/data/factions/malazan/ai.json` and `.../whirlwind/ai.json`, `difficulties.hard.gatherBonus` (0.4; 0.25 to go back), or an inbox note ("Hard back to 25%", "Hard 50%"); the data track re-measures the tally and re-pins the Hard matches.

### Units are drawn at the size their data says (the Teblor's 1.5× when they arrive), while clicks and collisions keep the real size (view track, M7-V1, 2026-11-10-0146, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** The screen now honours the per-unit `scale` the sim gained last session: a unit's body (the placeholder capsule), its green selection ring, the red attack-target ring, its health bar, the corpse disc and the spell cues round a caster all grow or shrink with the scale; the minimap dot does not. The scale is applied once when a unit type's mesh is built, so drawing a mixed crowd costs nothing extra (300 units of mixed sizes: 0 bytes a frame). **Nothing in the shipped data has a scale yet, so the game looks exactly as before** (QA compared screenshots pixel for pixel against last week's build). A forged test copy with a 1.5× Heavy Infantry, a 0.5× Crossbowman and a 3× Sapper was screenshotted and looked at.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing until the Teblor roster lands (data track, after the sim makes room for a third faction): then a Teblor Warrior stands a head and a half over a Malazan soldier, with a longer health bar over it. Click where the unit *really* is: a giant's drawn upper body does not select it (see rough edges).

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **A bigger drawing is not a bigger click target**: selecting and box-selecting use the collision radius at the unit's feet, so a 1.5× unit is no easier to click or to right-click-attack than a 1× one. The alternative (click anywhere on the drawn body) is a small view change if a playtest wants it. (b) A small unit's health bar never shrinks below three quarters of the normal length (a 0.5× unit's bar stays readable; a 3× unit's is 3× long); the bar's thickness never scales, so the cast bar and status markers stacked over it keep their spacing.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1177 (S4):** arrows and hit flashes leave from and land at a fixed 1.2 m, so a 0.5× unit shoots from above its head and a 3× unit is hit at the knees; and with decision (a) a 1.5× unit's top third is not clickable at the closest zoom (a playtest will probably notice; say "click the whole body" in the inbox to change it). Both in the view's next task. **BUG-1178 (S3, not this task's):** one view test scene (`QaM6V18Test`) has been red since last session's save-format change; the game is unaffected; the view's next task fixes the scene.

**How to change it.** A unit's `scale` in its `units.json` (0.5-3.0; 1 = as today); the health-bar floor is `CombatViews.BarMinScale` (0.75) in `game/scripts/CombatViews.cs`; or an inbox note.

### The war-dog pack's rules exist: one order trains three dogs at once, and a unit can carry a "slow on every bite" passive; nothing shipped uses either yet (sim track, M7-2, 2026-11-10-0146, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** Two generic rules for the Teblor's unique unit, as data hooks any faction could use. (1) **A multi-spawn queue item** (`spawnCount`, 1-8): one order, one queue square, one price and one build time, and at the end N units walk out together. Population is per dog: a pack of three at 1 pop each takes 3 slots, all reserved the moment the item starts (so a pack starts only when all three fit; cancelling refunds everything). The pack spawns all at once or not at all that tick: with only two free cells at the door it waits a tick rather than standing two dogs and owing one. (2) **An on-hit passive** (`onHit`: a status, a strength, a duration): every blow or arrow the unit lands on a *surviving* enemy applies the status to it (Hamstring: Slowed 20% for 2 s, refreshed by each bite, so a kited enemy can't outrun the giants). It never fires from splash damage, burning, a tower's shot, or the hit that kills. Tested on copies of today's data only; no shipped unit, file or fingerprint changed; no save-format change; the AI's population triggers already count a started pack.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet. When the Teblor roster lands: order a War-dog pack at the Stables & Kennels and one square appears in the queue; 24 seconds later three dogs run out to your rally point in a fixed order; bite a fleeing archer and it slows to 80% speed for 2 seconds after each bite.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) All-or-nothing spawning (above) rather than one dog at a time, which would have needed a bigger save format. (b) A pack that doesn't fit the population cap is paid and waits unstarted at the head of the queue, as any unit does today; there is no "not enough population" refusal at the order. (c) A bite on a unit already under a *stronger* slow (a Sandstorm's 50%) keeps the stronger slow and only extends it, by the status store's existing rule; so sustained bites keep a Sandstorm slow on indefinitely (worth remembering for the Teblor balance pass). (d) **Blood-oil Frenzy's aftermath slow is deferred** to its own task: it needs a "when a status ends, apply another" hook and a decision about the store's one-entry-per-status rule (a Zealot's own Frenzied must not slow it when it ends; only the Shaman's).

**Rough edges (all latent, nothing shipped triggers them).** **BUG-1167 (S3):** a pack whose total population is above the match's hard cap (say 8 dogs at 13 pop) loads without complaint and then sits paid and unstarted for ever; it should be a load error. **BUG-1168 (S3):** the AI and the end-of-match army-value graph count each dog at the whole pack's price (three dogs of a 120-gold pack count as 360), and the AI's queue census counts a pack as one unit; the design doc's sentence about the attack threshold was corrected. Both are the sim's next task, before the war-dog row ships. **BUG-1169 (S2, fixed at the merge):** one QA test pinned the data fingerprint as a literal the same session the data track moved it; the Producer's two-line patch made it dynamic. **BUG-1170 (S3):** four speed-gate tests fail on this PC even before this session's code (the machine is running slow after hours of three-track testing); re-measured cold next session.

**How to change it.** The Teblor war-dog row, when it lands: `game/data/factions/teblor/units.json` (`spawnCount` 3, `pop` 1, `cost` 120 / 0, `trainTime` 24, the `onHit` passive `slowed` 0.2 for 2 s); the pack cap is `DataLimits.MaxSpawnCount` (8); or an inbox note ("dogs spawn one by one", "Hamstring 3 s").

### Units can heal on their own now (regeneration) and can be drawn bigger than they are (a visual size per unit), both built as rules with nothing using them yet; and because of it, every save and recording from before this session is gone (sim track, M7-1, 2026-11-09-2226, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** M7 (the Teblor faction) opens with its two generic rules, built first so the content can come later as data only. (1) **Regeneration.** A faction can now say in its data file "my units heal 1 hit point a second, starting 6 seconds after the last time they were hurt" (the Teblor page's numbers; the Andii page says 1.5 a second after 5). Every hit, arrow, splash, friendly-fire hit or burn restarts the wait. The healing is exact: 1.5 a second is three hit points every two seconds for ever, no rounding drift, never above the unit's maximum (an hp upgrade researched mid-heal raises the ceiling and the unit keeps healing to it). There is also a "Regenerating" status that a spell or a zone can put on a unit: it heals through the wait and adds to the faction's rate while it lasts (this is the hook the Andii Darkness zone will use in M9). A match where nobody regenerates costs nothing extra and plays exactly as before: every recorded test match, every pinned digest and the test recording's checkpoints are unchanged. (2) **A visual size per unit** (`scale`, 0.5 to 3): the Teblor are drawn 1.5× while their collision stays normal. Only the data and the view read it; the sim ignores it (2,500 units of mixed sizes play tick-for-tick as the same units at size 1). (3) **Half-step population proven end to end**: a 1.5-pop unit is refused when you are half a slot short, the cap bar prints "9.5", and the AI counts the half in its own decisions (this already worked since M3; now it is tested through production, the cap and the AI). (4) The `giant` armor class (Teblor) is proven against the shipped damage table: ×1.25 from pierce and magic, ×0.75 from siege.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet: no faction in the game has a `scale` or a `regen` value, and nothing applies the Regenerating status. When the Teblor roster lands (the data track, after its Hard-tuning task), a Teblor warrior that walks out of a fight starts healing after 6 seconds, about one hit point a second, so you cannot wear them down with a trickle of arrows; and they stand head and shoulders over everyone else once the view's half (M7-V1, next session) draws them at 1.5×. **What you will notice now, and it is the one thing to act on:** *every save and every recording you made before this session refuses to load or play* ("another format" for saves, "made with other game data" for recordings), because the save file gained a section and the data's fingerprint moved. New saves and recordings work exactly as before. I chose a single save format for every match (the previous five special cases are gone) rather than keep readers for the old ones; a hobby game with no released build does not need old-save compatibility yet, and it removes a tangle of version branches.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The faction's healing waits the delay after every hit; the status heals through it** (the Teblor and Andii pages say "after N seconds without damage"; a spell that says "heals" should not stop the moment the unit is poked). (b) **Rates are written in hit points per second and kept in steps of 0.05**; a rate off the step (say 0.07) is quietly rounded (BUG-1166: the alternative is to refuse it at load the way a bad population value is refused; cheap to change). (c) **Save format 10 for every save, older ones refused** (above). (d) **The visual size is presentation only**, range 0.5-3 (a model half or three times its template is still readable; the Teblor buildings' 1.25× is a models-task matter, not this field).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1165 (S4):** a hand-edited save file with an impossible "last hurt" time or a wrong count of regenerating units still loads (no game ever writes one; the next sim hardening tightens the check). **BUG-1166 (S4):** the silent rounding above, and a status rate at an exact half-step boundary (0.175) can round one unit differently from the same faction rate; no shipped value is affected. Both are listed for the next sim hardening (counter 1 / 4).

**How to change it.** A faction's healing: `game/data/factions/<id>/faction.json` `regen: { "hpPerSecond": 1, "delay": 6 }` (leave it out for none). A unit's size: `units.json` `scale` (0.5-3, default 1). The status's name and text: `game/data/common/statuses.json` `regenerating`. Or an inbox note ("Teblor heal faster", "no delay for the Andii", "refuse off-step rates").

### AI-against-AI matches finish properly now: a beaten AI stops rebuilding houses it doesn't need, and the winner's army checks the map's empty start locations before combing the whole map; the sim side of M5 is complete and hardened (sim track, M5-H6, the end-of-M5 sim hardening, 2026-11-09-1336, ACCEPTED after one fix round)

**What was built.** Three fixes to how an AI-against-AI match ends. (1) **The house rule.** When an AI loses a house it used to rebuild it at once, every time, even with three workers and no army left; a beaten AI could put up a hundred tents over an hour, each one a fresh target that kept the winner's army busy. Now a lost house is rebuilt only when the AI actually needs the room (its population is within 2 of its cap, the same test it uses to build a new house in the first place). (2) **The hunt checks the empty start locations.** Since last session a beaten AI often has a last depot and a few workers at a far corner of the map (the far-gold expansion). The winner's army used to comb the whole map nearest-first and reach that corner last. Now, from its second hunt of a match on, it goes first to the start locations no player holds (nearest first), then to an enemy's own start, and only then combs the rest. The first hunt is unchanged (it starts where the enemy was beaten, which is usually where the remnant is). (3) **The far-gold leg is capped and bounded.** A worker sent to look at a far start location that gets killed on the way is replaced at most twice per match (the same cap the AI's scout has); past that the AI stops sending workers to die at a guarded corner. And the AI only walks to start locations within its 384 m reach, since a mine farther away would never be used anyway.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing changes until an AI is beaten. Then: play on Pale Hills against a Normal AI, raze its base, and it will no longer re-tent its ruins endlessly; and when you watch an AI-against-AI match (set both slots to AI, Pale Hills), it now ends in 41-46 minutes on every seed instead of 66-80 minutes or never. The numbers: the two Pale Hills test matches that had slipped past the hour now end at 41:18 and 46:14; the match between a Hard and a Normal AI, run 42 times across the three maps, ends 40 times inside the hour (was 37) with Hard winning 29, Normal 11, two unfinished (one long war Normal wins at 97 minutes). The 20-minute proof match on Vathar Crossing still ends inside 20 minutes (19:26). Your own saves, recordings and matches play exactly as before (the recording check is unchanged; no save-format change).

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The house rule is in**, reversing my own call of 2026-11-08 to keep it out; back then a rebuilt house was the beacon the winner's army found, and without it two test matches never ended. With the far-gold expansion and the hunt's new start-location check, every pinned match ends sooner with the rule than without, so it ships. (b) **Two clauses of my own brief were waived as brief mistakes, not code faults.** I had asked for "Hard ahead of Normal on every map": Hard is level with Normal on Vathar Crossing (7 wins each), exactly as it was before this task, and nothing in this task touches a Vathar match (they are decided before any hunt starts). That is a Hard-tuning job for the data track (BUG-1163, now S3, queued). I had also asked that eight old test recordings still reproduce with the new AI features switched off; the two rules above have no off-switch (they are bug fixes, and I had ruled out new knobs), so six of the eight now pin today's play with the old values kept in comments (BUG-1164, closed). Rule 48 in the handoff keeps me from writing such clauses again. (c) **The leg cap counts the AI's total losses in the match, not leg deaths** (a per-leg count would need a save-format change); late in a match this means the first leg death ends the leg for good. Accepted as a known limit. (d) **Not shipped, measured:** a "look near where the hunt began before the long perimeter walk" lever (adds nothing once the other two are in) and a "go for the loser's drop-offs first" lever (it made a Raraku match take twice as long).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1163 (S3):** Hard only ties Normal on Vathar Crossing; the data track's next-but-one task tunes Hard's numbers. **BUG-1161 (S4):** three small ones (the reach check reads a start's centre, not its nearest mine; on an odd-shaped map a hunt's stand-in point for a start can be out of sight of it; a lost house can be rebuilt twice in a row); none shows on the three shipped maps; the next sim hardening. **BUG-1151 (S3):** a four-AI free-for-all on Pale Hills now runs into an older bug (a Gather order re-sent to an empty mine every half second); harmless in play, a skipped test row. **One Pale Hills four-AI free-for-all (seed 1) still never ends:** with four seats there is no free gold on the map (BUG-1068 / 1116). The Malazan page's prose above two tables still quotes the old defeat times the sim re-printed (the data track's next task).

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.houseWhenPopWithin` (2: how close to its cap the AI must be before a lost house is rebuilt), `ai.scoutReplacements` (2: the shared cap for the scout and the far-gold leg), `ai.farExpandReach` (384). The hunt's start-location check has no knob; say "hunt: no start check" in the inbox to have one added or the rule removed.

**Try it:** `dotnet run --project tools/Rts.Cli -- match --map pale_hills --seed 2` plays the once-stuck Pale Hills match headless in about two minutes and ends `result winner p1 at tick 49565 (41:18)` with `hunts 3`; `--seed 5` ends at 55,485 (46:14).

### Both faction pages now explain how the AI adapts to you, in the owner's words; no game number changed, and the "counter shift" is measured where it shows and where it can't (data track, D26a, 2026-11-09-1336, ACCEPTED, 0 fix rounds)

**What was built.** A new sub-section "How the AI adapts" on `docs/factions/malazan.md` and `docs/factions/whirlwind.md` (under "AI build order (Normal)", before the first opening), describing in plain words the three AI rules that landed this week: the counter shift (the AI remembers the enemy soldiers it has seen, by kind, for 180 s, and tilts its training toward what answers them: Easy not at all, Normal half strength, Hard full), the starved charge (an AI that can't afford its next soldier for 60 s attacks with what it has), and the far expansion (an AI out of gold sends a worker to the unused start locations and builds a Quartermaster's Depot / Supply Cache, 0 gold / 75 wood, by a free mine within 384 m). Every number and name in the text is pinned to the data files both ways (`Content/AiAdaptsContentTests`, 25 cases; QA added 14 more): change a value in `ai.json`, `rules.json` or `buildings.json` without the page, or the page without the data, and a test reads red (I checked one mutation myself: "Normal 0.6" on the page fails the pin). **No `game/data` file changed; the data hash is unmoved.**

**Review table.** No unit, building or tech changed. New text (the two paragraphs are for you to read, not in-game text): the full sub-sections are on the two pages; the Malazan one opens: "Counter shift: the AI remembers how many enemy soldiers of each slot it has seen at once (workers never count, and it sees only what its own fog of war shows), and that memory fades to nothing over `rules.json` `ai.counterMemory` 180 s unless a sighting at least as big renews it. ... A Malazan AI that has seen only cavalry weighs its Heavy Infantry ×1.5 on Normal and ×2 on Hard. The shift tilts the army, it doesn't replace it." and the "What answers what" bullet lists each faction's answers per enemy kind (Malazan: Line → Cadre Mage, Catapult; Ranged → Wickan Lancer; Shock → Heavy Infantry; Caster → Wickan Lancer, Crossbowman; Siege → Heavy Infantry, Wickan Lancer; Whirlwind: Line → Priest of the Whirlwind, Battering Ram; Ranged → Horse Raider; Shock → Raider; Caster → Horse Raider, Desert Archer; Siege → Raider, Horse Raider).

**BUG-1156 measured (where the shift doesn't show), nothing committed.** The scene: a Hard Malazan AI watches 20 Horse Raiders for three minutes. (C) As shipped: it trains 11 Heavy Infantry and 8 archers having seen them, 11 and 9 not having: the shift is invisible, because its one Legion Barracks already trains a Heavy Infantry every time its queue empties and wood, not weight, is the limit. (A) A second Barracks step added to the Malazan opening at the time the first wave is due: it lands at about 8 minutes, no change to the count, and it costs the `standard` opening its 20-minute matches against two Whirlwind openings (defeated at 13:35 and 19:26). (B) A Line counter in the Age I mix: not buildable (the only Malazan unit that answers cavalry is Heavy Infantry already). **Recommendation, which I take as the Producer default: (C), no data change**; the design doc now says in one sentence that the shift shows only when the bank, not a saturated producer, is the limit (my edit at ACCEPT). **Your question: keep Normal 0.5 / Hard 1.0, or stronger?** My default is keep: a stronger value changes nothing in Age I while the barracks is saturated, and in Age II the ×2 already doubles the weight. Write "counter strength: Normal 0.75 / Hard 1.5" (or any pair) in the inbox to change it; the data track re-measures the pinned matches with it.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1181 (S3, docs only):** the far-expansion sentence (copied from the design doc) read as if a mine at a start location qualifies at any distance; the AI applies the 384 m reach to every mine. I fixed the design doc's sentence at ACCEPT; the two pages' sentence is the data track's next task (D-R35), with the S4 nits ("Three rules" introduces five bullets; the pin accepts a number that happens to equal a pinned value; a failure message prints '' for "none"). The sim's hardening this session re-printed ten table cells on the pages (allowed); the Malazan prose above two of those tables still quotes the old times: D-R35 too.

**How to change it.** The text: edit the pages (the pin tells you if a number disagrees with the data). The numbers: `game/data/factions/<id>/ai.json` `difficulties.<d>.counterStrength`; `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.counterMemory` / `ai.starvedWaveAfter` / `ai.starvedMinArmy` / `ai.farExpandReach`; or an inbox note.

### The AI goes for the map's far gold when its own runs out, and with that the adapting AI and the last charge of a broke AI are in the game (sim track, M5-9b + M5-9a, 2026-11-09-0426, ACCEPTED after one fix round; M5 criterion 9 ticked, only your playtest left)

**A detour worth knowing about.** At my first check, one test-hygiene guard was red on the branch: QA's own new test file measures memory allocation and had forgotten the one attribute that keeps such measurements from running beside other tests (BUG-1160). `main` must stay green and I do not edit tests, so I rejected the branch for that line, asked for a fix round, the one attribute went in, QA re-checked, I re-ran the whole default test loop on a fresh copy (8,245 green), and then accepted. Nothing in the game changed by that detour; it cost about an hour and a new rule for QA (run the default loop with your own files in).

**What was built.** The last piece of the held AI work: an AI whose gold is spent now goes and takes the map's unclaimed mines. Every half second each AI asks: am I short of gold for the soldier I'd train next, with no worker on gold and no gold mine I know of that I could still dig? If so it "arms": it sends one worker to walk to the nearest start location nobody is playing from (the game shows every start location in the setup screen, so this is map knowledge, not cheating; it still has to *see* a mine there before it may use it) and look round it; the moment it has seen a free gold mine with no enemy depot beside it, it builds its cheapest depot that costs no gold next to the mine (the Malazan depot or the Whirlwind supply cache, 75 wood; a full Town Hall only if it happens to be able to pay for one) and its workers move to the new mine. One expansion at a time; if gold starts coming in some other way the worker is called back. A data knob sets how far it will go (`ai.farExpandReach`, 384 m: anywhere on a 256 m map; 0 turns it off). Saves carry the state. **With it, the whole held branch landed:** the AI that remembers what you field and tilts its army toward the counter (Hard fully, Normal half, Easy not at all), and the broke AI's last charge (a minute without any way to buy a soldier and it attacks with what it has).

**What you will see or feel.** Play on Pale Hills to the 25-minute mark and watch the AI's base: when its two home mines are empty, a lone worker walks off toward an empty corner of the map, and a few minutes later a depot stands by the far mine with workers streaming to it; the AI keeps training instead of going quiet. On Raraku and Vathar Crossing you will rarely see it (their home mines last). Against a Hard AI, build mostly cavalry and within a few minutes its waves carry more spearmen; swap to archers and it drifts toward cavalry. A beaten AI with no income makes one last charge instead of sitting still. **The AI-against-AI test match on Pale Hills now ends at 40:42** (it was a stalemate, then a 57-minute slow raze); the other maps' test matches play exactly as before.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The Pale Hills test match's bound is an hour now, not 30 minutes.** You said nothing in the inbox, so my default ran: build the expansion first, then apply the rule I had written down: a finish between 30 and 60 minutes means the bound becomes an hour and the old "never ends" bug (BUG-1153) becomes a small known one. The 30-minute bound was my own earlier decision, so no decision of yours was reversed. (b) **A depot, not a Town Hall, at the far mine:** a broke AI can never pay 275 gold for a hall, and the design doc already says the camp exists so workers need not build a hall at an expansion. (c) **The AI may read the list of start locations** (it is on the setup screen for everyone), never what stands at one. (d) **Every difficulty expands,** Easy included (one knob, no per-difficulty setting); with Easy expanding too, two Easy-against-Normal test matches on Pale Hills changed their recorded play, as expected. (e) The far expansion is not paused during a raid: a raid that idles every gold worker may send one worker off on a walk; it comes back once gold flows again. The alternatives you could still pick: "more gold on Pale Hills" (a map change, so the AIs rarely need to expand there), "Easy never expands" (a per-difficulty knob), "the far expansion should build a hall" (slower, costlier, but a second base that can train).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1157 (S3):** on Pale Hills some *decided* AI-against-AI matches now take longer to finish: the loser has far gold to rebuild from, so the winner's hunt spends longer finding its last buildings; two recorded test matches (seeds 2 and 5) run past the hour (ended at 66 and 80 minutes), and in 42 Hard-against-Normal matches five on Pale Hills (Hard winning each) had not finished at the hour where before none were open. Hard still wins 26 of 42 to Normal's 11; the AI is not weaker, its matches are longer on that one map. This is the next sim hardening's first item (the hunt's sweep order and the loser's rebuild churn, the older BUG-1116). **BUG-1158 (S3):** if an enemy guards every free start location, the AI keeps sending workers there one after another until it has none (seen only in a scripted test; in real matches at most one worker was lost on the walk); the hardening caps it as the scout's replacements are capped. **BUG-1159 (S4):** three small ones (the walk ignores the reach setting; a start cut short is walked again; a test's wording). **BUG-1156 (S3, from last session):** against a Hard AI whose one barracks is already busy, the tilt toward spearmen can show as one archer fewer rather than more spearmen; the data track's next task (D26) looks at the openings for that. **Saves:** a save of a match against the AI made before this session will refuse to load (the AI's memory is now in the save); saves of human-only matches and every recording still play.

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.farExpandReach` (384; 0 = off), `ai.starvedWaveAfter` (60 s) / `ai.starvedMinArmy` (1), `ai.counterMemory` (180 s), `ai.counters`; per difficulty `game/data/factions/<faction>/ai.json` `counterStrength` (0 to 1); or an inbox note ("Easy never expands", "the far expansion builds a hall", "Normal should barely adapt", "more gold on Pale Hills").

**Try it:** `dotnet run --project tools/Rts.Cli -- match --map pale_hills --seed 1` plays the Pale Hills test match headless in about 90 s and ends `result winner p1 at tick 48858 (40:42)`; the five-minute lines show both sides' gold climbing past 9,000 after 25:00 (the far mines), where before they stopped at about 9,000.

### The AI that adapts its army to yours is built but held back one session: with it, one of the test matches between two AIs never ends, so I sent it back for the fix rather than ship it (sim track, M5-9a round 1, 2026-11-08-1316, REJECTED; **round 2, 2026-11-08-1556: the fix works, the match now ends but too late, held again; landed with M5-9b on 2026-11-09-0426, see the entry above**)

**Update, round 2 (2026-11-08-1556, ESCALATED).** **What was built on top:** a broke AI now attacks with what it has. Every second it checks: can I pay for the soldier I'd train next? If not, is the thing I'm short of (gold or wood) something I can still get (a worker on it, or a mine or forest I know of within reach of a depot)? If not, and I still have at least one free soldier, I am "starved"; after a minute of that (a data knob, `ai.starvedWaveAfter`, 60 s; 0 turns it off) my whole army goes, whatever its size, and if I know no enemy building I hunt. A raid on my base never counts as starvation, and getting an income again clears it. It applies to every difficulty; saves carry the timer. **What it did:** three AI-against-AI matches that used to stall for ever now end (Pale Hills seed 2 in 45 minutes, its four-AI version in 67, Raraku seed 5 in 44), and the Pale Hills seed 1 match that caused the hold is no longer a stalemate: it ends at **57 minutes**. **Why it is still held:** that match's test bound is 30 minutes. At minute 30 the loser has no army left but 29 workers and a dozen buildings it keeps rebuilding with 4,000 wood, and the winner has ten archers and no gold; archers raze slowly. The real cause is older (BUG-1068): both AIs spend their start mines by minute 24 and nobody goes for the map's far gold, 260 m away, because the AI's "expand" step only looks 40 m. No setting of the new timer changes that (I had 30 / 60 / 120 s measured: no end / 57 min / 60 min). **What QA found and fixed in the round:** the first version let a side off the hook if it could still gather *something*, even when nothing it could gather would ever buy a soldier (BUG-1154, fixed), and a timer of 0.01 s silently meant "off" (BUG-1155, fixed). **What QA found and left (BUG-1156, S3):** when the Hard AI's one barracks is already turning out a spearman every time its queue empties, "weigh spearmen double" cannot add any; the shift shows only when money, not the building, is the limit; so against a Hard AI you may see one archer fewer rather than more spearmen until the data or the openings change (a second barracks step, or a queue preference: D26's call). **Why I did not just raise the bound to an hour myself today:** I set that bound and my brief said no re-bound and no skip; the rows are red and `main` must stay green; and the rule that the same task is not sent back a third time means the next step is yours to confirm. **Your choice is the first item under Waiting on you**, with my default (fix the expansion, then land it all under a pre-written rule: if the match ends between 30 and 60 minutes once the AIs expand, the bound becomes an hour and this becomes a small known bug; if it still never ends, I stop and ask again). **How to change it:** `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.starvedWaveAfter` (60) / `ai.starvedMinArmy` (1); an inbox note ("starved after two minutes", "Easy never does a last charge").

**Round 1 (2026-11-08-1316), as written then:**

- **What was built (on its own branch, not in the game yet):** the AI now remembers, per kind of unit (line, ranged, cavalry, casters, siege), how many of yours it has seen at once, only through its own fog of war (an ally's shared sight counts, a hidden base does not), and forgets a sighting over three minutes. When it picks the next soldier to train it leans toward what counters what it remembers: Hard leans fully (Line weighs double against an all-cavalry army), Normal half as much, **Easy not at all** (Easy plays exactly as today). It never drops a unit from its usual mix or adds one it doesn't normally build; it tilts. Saves against an AI carry the memory (a new save format; your old AI saves will refuse to load once it lands, as with every AI change; human-only saves are untouched).
- **Why it was sent back:** the studio's five timed AI-against-AI matches are the guard rail for "the AI finishes a game". With the tilt, the Pale Hills match on seed 1 stops ending: both AIs spend every gold mine near their bases by minute 24 and never go for the far ones (an older weakness, BUG-1068), and the side left with ten archers sits under its "attack when I have this much" line for ever, while still knowing an enemy building exists, so it never switches to hunting either. The tilt didn't cause the poverty, it only changed who was left holding what, but a guard rail that goes red is a stop. The developer offered to ship it with the red row marked as a known bug, or to turn Normal's tilt down to a tenth (then it ends again): I refused both. A tenth would make the feature invisible, and at a quarter the match ends at 43 minutes, so the end game is brittle at any setting.
- **What happens next (next sim session, same branch):** a starved AI attacks with what it has: when it has no gold income, can't afford its cheapest soldier and still has an army, it waits a short while (a data knob, about a minute) and then launches with what it has instead of sitting. That is the AI change the older bug already recommended, it applies to every difficulty (an Easy stalemate is still a stalemate), and the full stress pass runs on top. If that doesn't end the match either, I'll stop and bring you the choice (a wider expansion reach, or map data).

On Normal the lean is half as strong; on Easy nothing changes. You'll also see a poor, beaten AI make a last charge rather than wait to be found.
