### The AI-against-AI proof is in: a Normal AI beats a Normal AI on Vathar Crossing in 19 minutes with every error check on, each map has its own timed match, and you can run the same match from a prompt (sim track, M5-5, 2026-11-08-0726)

**What was built.** M5's fifth criterion reads "an AI-vs-AI headless match of 20 minutes completes without errors and one side wins". The game could already do that; what was missing was the committed, repeatable proof that runs every session. (1) **The match itself, as a permanent test.** Two Normal AIs (Malazan against Whirlwind) on Vathar Crossing, seed 1: the Whirlwind side wins at 18:59, and while it plays the test checks, twenty times a second, that nothing threw, that no AI saw through the fog, that each AI's count of enemy buildings matches what it has really seen (minus a beaten player's), that every unit and building is on the map with sane numbers, and that every order the AI gave which the game refused (a build on a spot a unit just stepped onto, an order to a soldier who died that instant) is of a kind we have written down and never repeats more than eight times on one target. This runs in the ordinary test loop, so every future change has to keep it green. (2) **The same match on each map in its own time:** Raraku ends at 23:24, Pale Hills at 28:30, the generated map at 18:09; plus a four-AI free-for-all (43:35) and a 2v2 (28:45). Each one plays identically in two separate processes, and the Vathar match saved at half time and loaded back plays to the same ending. (3) **A seam for the tests:** the game now reports, to tests only, why it dropped an order. In a real match this costs nothing and changes nothing; it is not saved and not part of the fingerprint your recordings check. (4) **A command for you:** `Rts.Cli match` plays any of these headless from a prompt.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing changes in a match you play: no AI rule moved, your saves and recordings still play, and every pinned match plays exactly as before. What you can do is run the proof yourself: open a terminal in the repo and type `dotnet run --project tools/Rts.Cli -- match --map vathar_crossing --seed 1`. In ten to twenty seconds it prints a line every five game minutes (who is still in, how much each side has gathered, army size), then `result winner p1 at tick 22794 (18:59)`, the number of attack waves and hunts, and which refused orders occurred (none on this map). `--map raraku`, `--map pale_hills`, `--map generated`; `--players 4 --teams 1,2,1,2` for a 2v2; `--ai hard,normal` to pit a Hard AI against a Normal one; `--record m.replay` writes a recording you can copy into the game's replay folder and watch from Main menu → Load Game. If no side has won by the limit (`--ticks`, default one hour) it says `result none` and exits with code 3, so a script can tell a stall from a win.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **What "a 20-minute match" means:** the literal proof is Vathar Crossing seed 1 within 20:00; the other maps get the same match with a documented bound each (30 minutes on Raraku and Pale Hills, 20 on the generated map, an hour for four AIs), because a Normal AI simply takes longer to finish on a 256-metre map with hedgerows, and a single 20-minute bar on every map would either lie or stall. (b) **"Without errors" is a fixed list**, checked on every tick, rather than "it didn't crash". (c) **Three kinds of refused order that the brief did not foresee are accepted as normal, not bugs:** a build the game refuses because it would wall off ground, a build whose spot an AI ally took in the same instant (2v2 only), and a worker sent to a mine the AI remembers but which has since been dug out. Each traces to a rule already written down, and none repeats (the longest run anywhere is one). (d) **The two real AI quirks the proof turned up were filed, not patched**, so the proof measures the AI as it is: see Rough edges.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1152 (S3):** on Raraku the losing AI, down to one worker, keeps it on gold although everything it could build needs wood, so it sits in silence for about five minutes before it is finished off (seeds 1 and 2); it still loses, and this only shows when an AI is already beaten. **BUG-1151 (S3):** on the generated map, seed 4, the AI re-sends one worker to an emptied mine twice a second for a minute; a wasted order, no stall. Both go into the next sim hardening (two or three sessions away). **Known and unchanged:** AI-only matches on Pale Hills seed 2 never end (BUG-1068, the gold runs out: a map or rule change for a later task); on the three hand-made maps seeds 3, 4 and 6 are the same match (the seed only picks the AIs' openings there). **How to change it:** "the proof match should be Raraku" or "the bound should be 15 minutes" are inbox notes (the bounds are constants in the test); "fix BUG-1152 now" moves it ahead of the hardening.

### The AI stops waiting on a beaten player's buildings and hunts instead; a team-mate AI aims just off your walls; a razed hall site goes back on its old spot, and one enemy unit on the ruins can no longer stop the rebuild (sim track, M5-H5 hardening, 2026-11-07-2306)

**What was built.** A hardening session: no new feature, four known problems closed and two measured and left open on purpose. (1) **A player who is out is forgotten.** The AI remembers enemy buildings it has seen even when it can't see them any more. When a player was knocked out of the match (no units and no production left: your win rule), its remaining buildings collapse, but the other AIs still "remembered" them, so a surviving AI too poor to send a full attack sat waiting for an attack it could never afford, aimed at buildings that no longer existed, and the match never ended. Now every AI forgets a beaten player's buildings the moment that player is out (the result banner tells everyone who is out, so this is no cheat), and goes hunting the real survivors. (2) **A team-mate's hunt aims just off your buildings.** In a team game, when an AI ally hunted an enemy it had last seen right against one of your buildings, it sent its army to that exact spot on your wall. It now aims half a metre clear of the building plus half a map cell, on its own side. Free-for-all and 1v1 play are untouched. (3) **A razed hall site goes back on the old spot.** If the AI's new Keep site was razed in the same moment it appeared, the AI thought the ground was bad and rebuilt one cell off. It now gives the old spot one more try. (4) **The bug that came with (3), found and fixed in the same session (BUG-1148):** the first version of (3) could be fooled by one enemy unit standing on the ruins: the AI would order the same refused Keep every half second for ever and never rebuild. Now one parked unit costs the AI one wasted order, then it builds a cell off. (5) Housekeeping: a test that had pinned a recording's fingerprint no longer does (BUG-1059); a saved game with a forged hunt index is refused.

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → Map → Pale Hills → Add player twice → Start, and let the AIs fight. When one AI is knocked out, the others no longer freeze: a survivor's army sets out across the map to find the remaining enemies within a few minutes of the defeat (QA: between one think and nine minutes after, in every match measured). In a 2v2 with an AI ally, its army no longer bunches against your walls when the enemy raids you; it stops just off your buildings. Raze an AI's Keep and park a soldier on the ruins: the AI tries the spot once, then builds its new Keep a few metres away rather than standing idle. **Your saves and recordings still play**: no save-format or data change, and every pinned match plays exactly as before.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **Forget a beaten player's buildings at once**, rather than only when seen collapsed: the defeat is public knowledge, and waiting for a look would be the same stall a minute later. (b) **The push off an ally's building is 0.5 m plus half a cell toward the hunter**, only in team games. (c) **One excused retry on the old hall spot**, carried in a field the saved order already had (no save change); the trade-off is a second razing of the site looks like a refusal and moves the hall a cell off (harmless). (d) **The "don't rebuild houses you don't need" rule stays out** (BUG-1116): I had it tried again with the fixes above in; it still makes the Pale Hills proof match run past its 36-minute bound (the winner's hunt finds the loser by its rebuilt houses, so without them a last production building hides for 20 more minutes) and turns another pinned match red. The losing side's house churn is a waste of its wood, not a stall, so it waits. (e) **The hunt's sweep order is unchanged** although it has a measured gap: a lone idle worker 75 m from where the hunt starts can be missed for 12 minutes because the army walks the whole map border first. Both re-orderings the developer measured fixed that case and broke two others QA has pinned (hidden workers found only on the second pass; the border walk on small maps). A proper fix needs its own task. (f) **Pale Hills seed 2's four-AI stall is now understood and left:** every AI runs out of gold by the 40-minute mark because the AI's "expand" step only looks for a mine within 40 m of its hall, and the map's two unused start positions (18,000 gold) are 260 m away. Fixing it is a rule change (expand toward any known unclaimed mine when gold is gone) or a map change (more or nearer neutral gold), for a feature session; say which you'd prefer if you have a view.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1149 (S3, pre-existing):** in a 2v2, an AI *defending* its base can still send defenders to an enemy standing against its ally's wall (the same situation as (2), through the defense rather than the hunt); harmless, the hunt's fix probably applies, next hardening or a rider. **BUG-1150 (S4):** if a human ally packs five or more buildings in a touching row, the push in (2) can walk the point along the whole row (an AI ally never builds that tightly). **BUG-1116 / BUG-1068 (S3):** as in (d), (e), (f): 4-AI matches on Pale Hills still end in only 6 of 12 free-for-alls and 8 of 12 team games within an hour; Vathar Crossing ends more often. Nothing in a match against you changes. **How to change it:** "rebuild houses only when near the cap" (BUG-1116), "expand to far mines when gold runs out" or "more gold on Pale Hills" (BUG-1068), "forget a beaten player's buildings only when seen" (a) are inbox notes; the ally clearance is a constant in the sim (`MilitaryManager.AllySlack`, 0.5 m), an inbox note if you want it a data knob.

### The Hard AI earns its name: it gathers a quarter faster, every soldier in reach turns on your weakest unit, and a badly hurt soldier walks home once instead of dying (sim track, M5-4c slice 2, 2026-11-07-0926)

**What was built.** The design has always said Hard plays "with tighter decisions" plus a 25 % gather bonus, and the data files have carried three switches for it since October (`gatherBonus`, `focusFire`, `pullBackWounded`), but nothing read them: until today Hard was Normal thinking twice as often with slightly bigger waves. Now all three work. (1) **The gather bonus:** a Hard AI's workers fill a load of gold or wood in four fifths of the time yours take (the walk and the drop-off are the same), so Hard's economy runs about a fifth ahead. (2) **Focus fire:** every half second, a Hard army that is fighting (its attack wave, or its defenders at home) looks at the enemy units it can see within each soldier's own striking distance, picks the one with the fewest hit points (a soldier before a worker), and every soldier that can reach it is told to attack that one; when it dies the next is picked. Soldiers that can't reach the pick keep fighting whoever is in front of them. (3) **Pulling back the wounded:** a Hard soldier in an attack wave that drops under 30 % of its health is sent home out of the wave; it is not counted as a loss (so the wave does not retreat because of it), it still defends the base, and it goes out again with the next wave, where it fights to the end. Easy and Normal are untouched: eight whole matches without a Hard seat play exactly as before, order for order.

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → set the AI slot to **Hard** → Start. Send a mixed group (say eight infantry and four archers) at a Hard army and watch the kill order: its soldiers all go for your most hurt unit in reach, so your weakened units die first and in a row, rather than everybody trading blows at random. Watch a Hard wave hitting your base: a soldier near death turns and walks home while the rest keep fighting; a minute or two later it is back in the next wave. Count your gold against Hard's at five minutes (Esc → the stats screen after the match): Hard's gathered total runs about 20-25 % ahead on the same number of workers. Normal and Easy play as last week. **Your saves and recordings still play**: no save-format or data change.

**Producer decisions (each "owner may revisit").** (a) **The wounded threshold is the one already in each faction's AI file** (`retreat.hpFraction`, 30 %), not a new global knob as my brief asked: both faction pages already describe it as "Hard pulls it back", and two knobs for one threshold would leave one dead. (b) **"Pulled back once, then it fights."** My brief said a wounded unit is never sent on a new wave. Built that way, Hard lost 10 of 18 matches to Normal (12 wins / 2 losses before the change): nothing heals in this game yet, so every pulled-back soldier was out for good and Hard's army shrank all match. The rule now is: pulled back the first time, and it goes with the next wave and stays; that gives 28 wins / 9 losses / 5 no result over 42 matches, against 27 / 10 / 5 before the knobs. When healing exists (a later milestone), the brief's rule becomes right again and this is one line to change. (c) **A soldier only focuses what it can strike** (its weapon range plus a step, capped at 14 m in `rules.json` `ai.focusReach`): the first build gave every soldier within 14 m the same target, and twenty infantry crowded round one Raider while the other nineteen Raiders cut them down (Hard lost a 20 v 20 that Normal wins with 14 left; it now wins it with 15 left). (d) **Soldiers before workers** in the pick, else an army in a base would switch from the soldiers hitting it to the nearest worker. (e) **Defenders focus only inside their own base** (a defender out in your base walks home first, as before). (f) **The gather bonus follows the seat's difficulty, not who controls it**, so a recording of a Hard AI plays back exactly as it was played; a seat you play is always Normal, so you never get the bonus.

**Rough edges.** (1) **Hard is as strong as before, not clearly stronger**, on the 42 matches we can afford to run: the gain from the three knobs is smaller than the swing between two matches, and even the gather bonus alone measures within that noise. Making Hard measurably harder than Normal (criterion 6's "lose to a Whirlwind AI on Hard") is a tuning task on a bigger sample, after M5's last two sim items; if you find Hard too easy or too hard in play, say so and it goes first. (2) **BUG-1120 (S3):** a Normal AI hunting the last enemies can aim at a spot on the edge of an ally's building where it last saw an enemy unit; harmless (it attacks no ally), fixed in the sim's hardening next session. (3) **BUG-1124 (S3, this PC):** the machine's processor slows to about half speed after a few seconds of hard work, so a speed test that runs right after another one reads slow; we now judge speed tests one at a time with a pause between (rule 42), and nothing in the game is slower (the Hard AI's think costs 0.73 ms for eight seats, under the 1 ms budget). **How to change it:** `game/data/factions/<faction>/ai.json` → `difficulties.hard.gatherBonus` (0.25), `focusFire` / `pullBackWounded` (true / false), `retreat.hpFraction` (0.3); `game/data/common/rules.json` → `ai.focusReach` (14); or an inbox note ("Hard's bonus 15 %", "no focus fire for Hard").

### Hover a difficulty in the skirmish setup and it tells you what that AI does; Hard's "25 %" is read from the data (view track, M5-V2, 2026-11-07-0926)

**What was built.** The Difficulty list in the skirmish setup showed three bare names. Now each item, and the list itself, has a tooltip with that difficulty's rules in plain words, and the Hard one fills in the gather bonus from the faction's AI file (so if you change the number in the data, the text follows). The three texts, which you may reword: Easy: **"Thinks every 2 seconds, follows its build order slowly, attacks in small waves, doesn't micro, uses abilities and expands late."** Normal: **"Fair play at a relaxed pace: follows its build order on time and uses abilities, but doesn't focus fire or pull back wounded units."** Hard: **"Fair play with tighter decisions: thinks every half second, focuses fire, pulls back wounded units, uses abilities well, and gathers 25% faster."**

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → hover **Easy**, **Normal** or **Hard** in an AI slot's Difficulty list (or the list itself): the sentence above, wrapped into a readable panel. Pick the other faction for that slot: the tooltip follows (both factions say 25 % today). This finished the design line "a 25 % gather bonus, shown in the skirmish setup", so **M5's difficulty criterion is ticked** together with the sim's knobs above.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1147 (S4):** "every 2 seconds" and "every half second" are typed in the text file, not read from the AI's think interval, so a tuning change there would leave the words stale; a few lines in the view's next session if you want the numbers live. The tooltip panel is still see-through over the Add / Remove buttons (the art pass's theme, BUG-1115 item 4). ### The AI rebuilds what it loses and looks before it attacks uphill; the two new maps' final sentences are in the game (sim track, M5-4d slice 2, 2026-11-07-0236)

**What was built.** Two behaviours the design asked for and the roadmap's criterion 3 was waiting on. (1) **Rebuilding.** Until now a building the AI lost stayed lost: a razed Barracks meant no more soldiers for the rest of the match, and a razed Town Hall meant its workers wandered with nowhere to drop their loads. Now, when a building the AI's build order put up is gone (razed, or its site cancelled), the AI orders it again within a think or two, with the same site search, the same saving-up rule and the same retry marks as the first time; it never builds more houses than it had, and a house is not rebuilt once the population cap is at the maximum. If the Town Hall itself is gone and a worker is alive, the hall comes before everything else: on exactly its old spot when that is free, else as near as a site is found, and while the AI can't pay for it yet it banks the cost (its army production spends only what is above it, its gatherers lean toward what it lacks). The spot is remembered across a save without any change to the save file. (2) **The look.** A wave sent against a building on higher ground than the army used to file blind up a ramp. Now it goes first to the top of the ramp nearest the target, on the target's own hill, and only then to the target: once a soldier reaches that ramp top, or the target comes into the AI's sight, or the wave is stuck, the attack order follows. On level ground, or against a target at or below the army's level, nothing changes. (3) **The two map sentences you reviewed last session** (Pale Hills, Vathar Crossing: the table in the D-H7 entry below) are now what the game shows; nothing else about those maps changed. (4) A small hunt bug fixed (BUG-1111: an army pulled far across the map by a sighting while walking the border no longer skips a stretch of edge).

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → Map → Pale Hills → Add player twice → Start. Raid an AI camp and raze its Barracks: a worker walks over and puts it back where it stood, and soldiers come out again a minute later. Raze its Keep instead: the next thing that AI builds is a Keep, on the same spot, before any house or soldier; its workers go back to gathering once it stands. On Vathar Crossing, hold a bank and watch an AI wave come up from the riverbed: it climbs to a ford's top first and pauses for a moment, then comes for your buildings. Hover **Pale Hills** and **Vathar Crossing** in the Map list: the final sentences. AI-against-AI matches on Pale Hills still end on seeds 1, 3-6 (seed 1 now at 28:30, a little earlier than last session, because the loser rebuilds and is found sooner). **Your saves and recordings from the last session still play**: nothing in the save or data fingerprint moved.

**Producer decisions.** (a) **The ramp top is the look point** (the developer's choice between the two rules the brief offered, accepted): the other rule could pick a point on the bank straight above the army that is reachable only through a ford elsewhere; the ramp top is where an attack up actually meets the high ground. On the two shipped maps the look fires rarely (the bases sit on each map's common level), so it mostly matters against a hill camp or when you fight from the riverbed. (b) **The old hall's spot is kept inside a field the save already holds** (as a negative number) rather than a new field: no save-format change, so your saves survive this session; the trade-off is a convention a future reader must know, written down in docs/03. (c) **A QA stress row that stopped ending is marked a known case rather than fixed here (BUG-1116):** on Pale Hills seed 2 with four AIs, the losing sides now rebuild houses they don't need until every side is out of gold, and the match has no result by two hours of game time. QA's proposed rule (rebuild a house only when the AI is near its population cap) was built in the fix round and **backed out**: it cut the churn but didn't end the match (every seat is broke by the hour mark: that is BUG-1068, a map-and-economy problem), and it made three other matches that used to end stop ending, because a rebuilt house is also what the winner's hunt finds. The slice ships; the hardening after next session takes it properly, in this order: (1) a defeated side's remembered buildings should be forgotten by its enemies (BUG-1119: that is what kept the one surviving AI from hunting), (2) the hunt should find a lone idle worker standing just outside a sweep point's sight, (3) the house rule re-measured with both in. (d) **Size:** about 1,150 hand-written lines against an 800 budget, accepted: the tests are the criteria's own rows.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1116** (S3) and **BUG-1119** (S3), above. **BUG-1118** (S4): a hall site razed in the same instant it appears makes the next rebuild go one cell off the old spot; the Malazan page's prose round the re-printed match times is stale (the data track's next task). A lost **expansion** is not rebuilt yet (only the main hall and build-order buildings are). A beaten AI's last worker now keeps rebuilding sites, so it is hunted a little later than before. **How to change it:** "don't rebuild houses" or "rebuild expansions too" are inbox notes; the look's hand-over distance is `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.rallyReach`.

### The AI finishes the match now: with no enemy building left to attack it hunts the enemy's last units across the whole map, so AI-against-AI games on Pale Hills end instead of stalling (sim track, M5-4d slice 1, 2026-11-06-0926)

**What was built.** Until now an AI army only ever attacked buildings: once it had razed everything it knew of, it marched home and sat at its rally point, and a beaten side's last worker hiding in the woods kept the match alive for ever (on Pale Hills, four of five seeds; the AI needs the units gone too under your win rule). Now, once the AI knows of no enemy building and has sent at least one wave, its whole army **hunts**, whatever its size: it goes to where it last saw an enemy unit (a worker counts) if that was within the last **two minutes** (`ai.huntMemory` in the rules, 120 s), otherwise it **sweeps the map**: a grid of points over the whole map (the same grid its scout uses, plus the corners between them, plus a ring of points along the map's edges), always the nearest point it has not yet walked to or seen, and when it reaches the edge it walks the whole border round once; every second lap it uses the points in between. Any enemy it sees on the way re-targets the hunt at once. A hunt ends as a wave does (heavy losses, a raid at home), and the moment an enemy building comes into view it becomes a normal attack again. The AI remembers only what its own fog shows it (QA checked every one of 16,702 sightings against the fog: no leak). A wave whose target is razed while no other building is known now turns into a hunt on the spot instead of going home. The hunt's memory is saved with the game, so **a save of a match against the AI is a new format (6 or 7)** and older ones refuse to load (they already did: the new rule moved the data fingerprint).

**What you will see or feel.** Start **Skirmish → Map → Pale Hills → Add player twice** and let the AIs fight (or `--skirmish --map pale_hills --players 4`): when a side's last building falls, the winner's army no longer walks home; it heads for the last enemy it saw, then combs the map, edge to edge, until the last worker is found, and the result banner comes up (QA's matches: a 4-AI free-for-all on Pale Hills ends in 46-54 minutes; a 2-AI match in 22-44). Against you nothing changes while you hold a building; if you lose your last one, your remaining units are hunted the same way. A hunt looks like a wave marching from point to point with attack-move orders; it never splits.

**Producer decisions.** (a) **One remembered point, not one per enemy** (the developer's call, accepted): the hunt follows one trail; a four-way free-for-all re-targets on whatever it sees next. (b) **Sweep points at the corners and along the border too** (not only the scout's grid): with the grid alone a unit standing between points, or within 10 m of the map edge, was never seen (sight is 14 m, the points 51 m apart on Pale Hills); QA proved it with workers hidden at the worst spots on all four maps, twice, and both gaps were closed (BUG-1107, fixed in the session). The cost: a lone army takes about 45 minutes to comb a 512 m map; splitting the army to sweep faster is a later slice if you want it. (c) **Two pinned measurements moved and were re-printed on the Malazan page** (two Malazan openings that used to stand beaten at 20:00 are now finished off at 10:24 and 17:18): the brief allowed it; I also re-wrote the paragraph around them so the page agrees with itself (the data track's two test allowances for those cases come out next session). (d) **A save with an AI seat from before this change is refused outright** rather than loaded without a hunt memory (the same rule M6-S4 used for teams). (e) Not taken: BUG-1067 (a side whose scouts all die at its door goes minutes without wood): neither quick fix was a few lines; it waits for the sim's hardening.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1068** narrowed: on Pale Hills seed 2 two Normal AIs still stalemate at 60:00, each holding two halls (not a hunt case: an enemy building is always known); the sim's hardening or slice 2. **BUG-1111** (S3): if the hunting army is pulled far across the map by a sighting while walking the border, it rejoins the border at the next ring point and misses the short stretch before it until its next lap (on the 512 m maps up to about 23 m of edge, where a hidden unit survives one more lap); planned as a rider of the sim's next task. The 36,000-tick proof match on Pale Hills (seed 1) now ends at 35,569 ticks, 21 s under the limit; it is deterministic, and the next hunt change re-measures it. **How to change it:** `game/data/common/rules.json` `ai.huntMemory` (seconds the AI trusts a sighting; 0 = only what it sees right now); "the hunt should wait for a wave-sized army" or "split the army to sweep" are inbox notes.

### Two more hand-made maps, Pale Hills and Vathar Crossing, are in the Map list, built from one quarter by a mirror tool so they are fair by construction; and the AI's scout cap now holds on any map (sim track, M6-S8, 2026-11-06-0326)

**What was built.** The roadmap's three hand-made maps are complete. **Pale Hills** (4 players, 256 by 256): four camps in the corners of a map of hedgerow woods, each camp an open clearing with two gold mines to its west and a woodlot to its north, joined to its two neighbours by narrow corridors between rows of trees; between each camp and the centre stands a hill with a knoll on top and ramps on three sides, and in the middle an open plaza. Timber is everywhere; gold is scarce beyond the camps (one extra pair of mines a camp, in a clearing on the east corridor). **Vathar Crossing** (2-4 players, 256 by 256): open steppe cut west to east by a sunken river bed 80 m wide, crossed only at four fords (a ramp down one bank and a ramp up the other); two camps on each bank, each with its mines and woodlot, and extra mines on the bank by the fords. The river bed is low ground, so an army down there cannot see the banks while the banks see it: holding a ford is holding a chokepoint. Both maps were drawn as **one quarter** and mirrored across both axes by a new developer tool (`mirror-map`), so every player's corner is the same shape and a 2-player match uses two diagonally opposite corners. Each was proven playable by a Normal AI against a Normal AI to a result (Pale Hills at 28:28, Vathar Crossing at 19:20), after retuning: Pale Hills' first draft starved both sides of gold, Vathar's first draft had the AI never finding its enemy. The scout cap from last session (**BUG-1057**) had a blind spot on 256 maps (a Town Hall sitting exactly on a point of the scout's search grid made the "this scout was a replacement" mark invisible); the mark is now laid half a metre off in that case, so the cap holds everywhere, with no change to the save format.

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → **Map → Pale Hills** → Add player twice → Start: you begin in the north-west clearing with a wide map of tree rows around you; expect long walks through corridors, armies arriving in a file, and little gold once your two mines are spent. **Map → Vathar Crossing**: your base on one bank, the enemy across the river; your first army walks down a ford, across the low river bed, and up the other side, blind to the banks on the way. A generated-map match is untouched (its recording plays identically). **Your recordings and saves from before this session refuse to play** ("another version": two map files joined the data).

**Producer decisions.** (a) **Vathar Crossing's 2-player starts are diagonal across the river**, not straight across: the AI assumes its enemy sits at the mirror of its own base through the centre, and the straight-across draft never found it; the tool now always orders starts so that start 1 is start 0's centre mirror. (b) **"Dense woods" is rows of trees with gaps, not solid blocks:** the game holds at most about 4,000 resource nodes a match (a capacity, not a rule), and Pale Hills uses 3,796 of them; solid woods would need a sim change nobody asked for. (c) **The two maps' sentences are provisional** (written by the sim developer to pass the data track's checks); the data track writes the final ones next session with a review table for you. (d) **The size budget** (BUG-1069): the map files themselves are generated content and do not count toward the task's line budget; recorded as a standing rule.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1068** (S3): a Normal AI against a Normal AI on Pale Hills reaches a result on seed 1 only; on seeds 2-6 within an hour the loser is razed to its last unit hiding in the woods (AI waves attack buildings only, so it is never hunted) or, on one seed, neither side breaks the other. Against you it ends when you finish them. The sim's next task (M5-4d) makes the AI hunt the last units and expand. **BUG-1067** (S3, pre-existing): if an enemy camps the AI's door and kills all three of its scouts in the first 20 seconds, the AI can go many minutes without cutting wood (its hall does not see its own woodlot 22 m away); planned with M5-4d or the next sim hardening. **How to change it:** the maps are text files, `game/data/maps/pale_hills.json` and `vathar_crossing.json` (edit the quarter under `tools/Rts.Cli/maps/` and run `Rts.Cli mirror-map`); a layout wish is an inbox note ("Pale Hills: more gold", "Vathar: two fords, not four").

### The AI stops feeding workers to an enemy camped at its door, looks once more for a forest it has never seen, and the studio's data edits no longer collide on the test recording (sim track, M6-SH1 hardening, 2026-11-05-2148)

**What was built.** Three things, none a new feature. (1) **A cap on scout replacements.** Last session's rule sent another worker out to scout whenever the first died before it had looked round home; an enemy camped at the AI's door could kill them one by one until the AI had no workers (BUG-1052). Now the AI sends a replacement only while it has lost at most **2 units in all** (`ai.scoutReplacements` in the rules), and only if the scout that died was itself a replacement, so the first death is always followed by one more try: three workers at most, then the AI assumes it has seen home and gets on with its economy. (2) **A second look for a missing resource.** If the scout dies after looking round home but the AI has still never seen a single forest (or mine), it sends one more scout within the same cap (BUG-1053); and a scout sent again, once it knows an enemy building, a mine and a forest, stops exploring and starts cutting that forest at once, unless that forest sits at the enemy's door (within the 16 m workers already flee at), because it is standing next to it and brings the first wood home sooner than a worker sent from the hall. (3) **The studio's test recording** (the "golden replay") used to carry the data's fingerprint in its header, and three tests insisted the header equal today's data, so every text or number change anywhere in the data forced a regeneration of the file, and two tracks changing data in one session collided on it (last session's D22 could not land for that reason). Now the recording's checkpoints are the proof and the header is just a label: a data change regenerates the file only when it changes the recorded match. Also: the "how many units a producer queues while spending a High start down" number is a rules knob now (`ai.spendDownQueue`, 2), a forged save with a walking unit that has nowhere to go is refused instead of crashing, and four small debt items (BUG-1049 / 1051 / 1054 / 0960) are closed.

**What you will see or feel.** In a normal match, nothing: the 25 pinned matches and the 27 opening pairings play identically (no scout dies in them). In the edge case, if you park soldiers at the AI's Town Hall from the first minute and kill each worker that walks out, the AI now loses three to that and keeps the rest working (it used to lose all of them). If its scout dies far out before seeing any forest, you may see one more worker leave to look. **Your recordings and saves from before this session refuse to play again** ("another version"): the data changed (two AI knobs, the presets' and Raraku's text).

**Producer decisions.** (a) **After the cap the AI assumes home is seen and gathers at the nearest nodes it knows** (rather than freezing its woodcutters until a scout succeeds): measured, no gatherer was sent farther than 32 m from the hall once capped, so nothing walks into the enemy base. (b) **The first scout's death always gets one more try**, whatever the AI lost before in a fight (QA found the first version counted every loss, so a base raided before its scout left never looked for a forest; fixed in the fix round). (c) **A start that sees no tree and loses every scout on its first tick gathers no wood** in the test's 5 minutes, and that is accepted: there is nothing it knows to walk to; the alternative (hold the reach) changes nothing there. (d) **"At the enemy's door" reuses the distance workers flee at (16 m)** instead of a new knob: one number fewer; if the edge case below wants a wider door, it gets its own knob then. (e) **The data track's regeneration of the recording this session was dropped at the merge**: unnecessary now, and a QA test pins the old header (BUG-1059).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1057** (S3): the "this scout was a replacement" mark is stored as a waypoint laid exactly at the hall's centre; if a hall's centre happens to be exactly a point of the scout's search grid, the mark is invisible and the cap is lost. No generated map ever puts a hall there (1,620 probed); a hand-made 256 map with starts at its quarter points would, so the fix rides with the next map slice (M6-S8). **BUG-1058** (S3): the released scout cuts or mines the node nearest *itself*, not the forest the door rule judged; in 8 of 25 cases that is a node within 16 m of an enemy building and 4 of those scouts die; still a net gain (more seats get wood by 5 minutes with the rule than without), so it waits for the next sim hardening. **BUG-1059** (S4): a test nit, the Producer's note above. **How to change it:** `ai.scoutReplacements` in `game/data/common/rules.json` (0 = never send a replacement; up to 8), `ai.spendDownQueue` (1-5); anything about the behaviour is an inbox note. **Update 2026-11-06-0326:** BUG-1057 is fixed (M6-S8: the mark is laid half a metre off when the hall sits on a grid point; QA proved the cap on all four quarter points of a 256 map); BUG-1058 / 1059 still wait for the next sim hardening.

### The skirmish setup has a Map list: pick Raraku and play, save, load and watch a match on the hand-made desert map (view track, M6-V18, 2026-11-05-2148)

**What was built.** The setup grid has a **Map** list beside the seed: **Generated** (the random map from the seed, size and counts, as before) or any hand-made map by name, today **Raraku**, with its description as the tooltip. Picking Raraku greys out Map size (it shows 128, the map's size), Forests and Gold mines (the map has its own), and caps the players at the map's two start positions: extra slots disappear, Add player greys out and a line says "Raraku has room for 2 players"; picking Generated again gives everything back. The match plays on Raraku, a save of it loads back onto Raraku (checked to the tick at ten seconds and three minutes in), a recording of it watches on Raraku, and Load Game's row says "; map: Raraku". The command line has `--map raraku` for dev runs. The rows were rearranged (Map size beside Map, Game speed beside Starting resources) so four players still fit a 648-high window.

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → **Map → Raraku** → Start: you start in the open desert on the west side with a mesa to your north; the enemy's camp is across the open centre, with few forests and long sightlines (the sentence under your cursor when you hover the list is the data track's, next entry; **on `main` today it is still the placeholder sentence**, because the data branch has not merged yet, see the note at the top of this file). Esc → Save, quit, Load Game: the row ends "; map: Raraku"; Load puts you back on Raraku; Watch replays your match on it. A generated match is untouched: same screen, same files, same rows.

If you would rather the rows vanish, say so. (b) **The slot cap hides the extra slots and disables Add player, with a line saying why**, rather than refusing Start with four slots; the picks of the hidden slots are kept and come back with Generated. (c) The map's description is a tooltip (as the presets'), not a line of its own: the setup is out of vertical room.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1092** (S3, command line only, the menu is safe): `--players 4 --map raraku` with team flags that put the two surviving players on one team starts a match that never ends (the one-team check runs before the player cap); fixed next view session. **BUG-1093** (S3): a one-off engine error in a test scene during the full 81-scene loop, 5 / 5 alone; a test flake, not the game. The greyed counts' misleading numbers, above. **How to change it:** the row's label, "Generated" and the "has room for" line are `setup.map`, `setup.map_generated`, `setup.map_players` in `game/data/common/ui.json`; the Load Game wording is `load.map`; Raraku's name and sentence are `game/data/maps/raraku.json`. **Update 2026-11-06-0326:** BUG-1092 is fixed and the greyed counts show the map's own numbers (M6-V19, the entry above); the list now holds Pale Hills and Vathar Crossing too. BUG-1093 waits for the view's hardening.

### Hand-made maps have a file format and the first one, Raraku, exists; the AI now looks round its own home before trusting what it sees far away; nothing to click yet, and your recordings refuse to play again (sim track, M6-S7, 2026-11-05-1716)

**What was built.** The roadmap's M6 wants three hand-made maps (Raraku, Pale Hills, Vathar Crossing) beside the random generator; until now every map came from a seed. A hand-made map is now **one text file** under `game/data/maps/` (`raraku.json` is the first): a grid of digits 0-2 for the ground's height (one character per cell, 128 rows of 128), a short list of ramps (rectangles that slope up toward north / south / east / west), the two to four start positions, the gold mines (each with its gold) and the forests (little pictures of `T` and `.`), plus a name and a description the player will read. When the game loads its data it checks every map the way it checks a generated one: both starts on the same level and at least half a map apart, two mines and a forest beside each, every ramp long enough to walk, no part of the map walled off; a mistake is reported as one error naming the line. A match on a hand-made map saves and records like any other (the file names the map; the old save and recording layouts are untouched: the studio proved a match on a generated map writes exactly the same bytes as before, twelve files compared). **Raraku** is a placeholder layout for now: open desert, your base west and the AI's east, a flat-topped mesa with a smaller butte on the north and the south flank, each reached by ramps, twelve mines and six small forests (a first draft with fewer starved both AIs, so the layout grew). A Normal AI against a Normal AI on it plays to a result (the Malazans win at 24 minutes). Before the map work, the two AI blind spots found last session were fixed (BUG-1047 / 1048): the AI's gatherers now stay within 64 m of home only until its scout has looked at the eight points round the Town Hall (about a minute to a minute and a half out), not until it has swept the whole map; a scout that dies before that is replaced by another worker instead of ending the scouting; and a scout's death no longer tells the AI "home is known".

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet: the setup screen has no Map list (the view's next task, M6-V18, this week); matches still play generated maps. When it lands, pick **Raraku** in the setup and you start in the open desert west with the mesa to your north. Against the AI you may notice it taking wood from a forest just past its old 64 m limit a few minutes earlier than before (it used to wait until the scout had crossed the whole map). **Your recordings and saves from before this session refuse to play** ("another version"), as every change to the game's data does.

**Producer decisions.** (a) **The map file is a picture, not a seed plus edits:** a text heightmap you can read and change in any editor beats a list of generator tweaks; the cost is a long file (128 lines of digits), which a small script wrote for Raraku. (b) **Hand-made maps obey the generator's start rules** (one level, half a map apart, two mines and a forest in reach) so the AI's openings, tuned on generated maps, work on them; a map that wants to break those rules (a mine-poor start, an asymmetric map) would be a design change for you to call. (c) **My own earlier decision was trimmed.** Last session I decided two things for the AI's reach: lift it once the scout has seen the ring round home (built), **and** while it holds, let a resource kind with no node in reach take the nearest known one anywhere. The developer built that second clause and measured it: it brought back the bug it was meant to help (with an ally's eyes the AI knows its ally's forests from the first second and walked its woodcutters 300 m to them), and a softer version sent woodcutters 170-195 m into the enemy's base; with the first clause alone the two bugs are fixed just as well. So the second clause is out; docs/01 says so. The alternative (keep it and add more exceptions) was more rule for no measured gain. (d) **A scout that dies before looking round home is replaced,** so a lost first scout doesn't leave the AI blind near home; the limit on how many times is the rough edge below.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1052** (S3, new): if every scout is killed the moment it leaves the hall (an enemy camped at the door, a tower rush), the AI keeps sending the next worker out to die and ends with no workers; a realistic camp of four soldiers on the ring costs it one scout, so this bites only in the extreme case. Fixed in the next sim session (the sim's hardening, first item: a cap of two or three replacements, then the AI stops waiting). **BUG-1053** (S3, not new): an AI whose scout dies after circling home but before it has seen any forest, on a start whose nearest forest is 90 m away, never sends another and gathers no wood; impossible on a valid map at the start (every start has a forest within 24 m), it needs the home forest cut down first; same session. **BUG-1054** (S4): docs/02 says the reach lifts in the scout's "first minute out" (measured: one to two minutes); a save of a Raraku match keeps the terrain in the save itself, the map's name in its header is a label. **How to change it:** edit `game/data/maps/raraku.json` (the digits are the ground, `T` the trees; the game refuses a map that breaks the start rules and says why in the log) or drop a second file beside it; the start rules themselves and the AI's reach are an inbox note. The maps' names and descriptions are the data track's next task; "Raraku" and its one-line description are placeholders until then.

### The rules now know two starting purses, Standard and High, and the AI spends a big start instead of sitting on it; nothing to click yet, and your recordings refuse to play again (sim track, M6-S6, 2026-11-05-1206)

**What was built.** docs/02 "Game flow" 2 says the skirmish setup offers starting resources, standard or high. The rules' half is in: `game/data/common/rules.json` now carries a list of **starting-resource presets** instead of one fixed purse: **Standard** (200 gold, 200 wood: exactly today's start, so every match played at Standard is bit for bit what it was) and **High** (1,000 gold, 1,000 wood); 5 workers either way. A match picks one preset for every seat (the same for all); the save file and the recording carry it, so a saved High match loads as High and a recording of one plays back right; saves and recordings in the older layouts read as Standard. The AI was then measured at High: two of its six openings (the Malazan "Fast Age II" and the Whirlwind "Holy war") sat on 1,000-1,800 of their 2,000 for the first five minutes, waiting for their build order's clock with full banks and idle barracks. So a High start also switches on a **spend-down rule** for the AI: while it holds more than 200 gold + wood together it brings its next timed build step forward (Age II, the later buildings), trains at every barracks (two units queued per building instead of one) and sends its gatherers toward whichever resource it is short of. At Standard the rule never fires (Standard has no threshold), so the AI you play today is unchanged: the studio replayed 20 matches and the 27 faction-page measurements against the previous build, identical.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet: the setup screen has no Starting resources list (next view session, M6-V17). When it lands, pick **High** and both you and the AI open with 1,000 / 1,000: expect the AI to reach Age II and its later buildings a few minutes earlier than at Standard and to field more units early, rather than banking the money. **Your recordings and saves from before this session refuse to play** ("another version"), as every change to the game's data does; anything recorded from this build on plays. New words the player will read, from `rules.json` (placeholders until the data track writes the final text next session): **"Standard"**, "Every player starts with the usual gold and wood."; **"High"**, "Every player starts with five times the usual gold and wood."

**Producer decisions.** (a) **The numbers:** Standard = today's 200 / 200, High = 1,000 / 1,000, workers 5 for both; one preset per match, no per-slot presets and no "Low" (both are taste calls I left to you: say "low preset 100 / 100" or "per-slot starting resources" in the inbox). (b) **The AI's spend-down threshold lives in the data, per preset** (`aiSpendAbove`, High 200), not in code: that is what keeps Standard untouched and lets you tune High alone ("aiSpendAbove 400" in the inbox, or edit the file). (c) **My own acceptance measure was restated.** My brief asked that at High no AI side bank more than twice what it banks at Standard at the 10-minute mark; QA showed that one 10-minute sample is noise (on 4 of 36 unseen matches a side held 160-480 at 10:00 over a Standard bank of 60-230, while spending everything in between) and that the real goal, "the AI spends its start", is met everywhere: averaged over minutes 2 to 10, a High bank is 0.3 to 1.4 times the Standard one on all 72 measured sides. The criterion is now that average (at most 1.5 ×); re-tuning the threshold to pass the old measure would have been fitting the number to the seeds. (d) **Recordings keep their old layout when nothing new is in them:** a Standard match is written exactly as before (so every reader of old recordings keeps working); only a High match uses the new layout.

**Rough edges.** BUG-1051 (S4, small notes): a stale comment in the Load Game list's reader (the view's next task), a test that still asserts the noisy 10:00 number on its own fixed seeds, and the "two per queue" count being a constant in code rather than a line in `rules.json` (the next sim clean-up). **How to change it:** the presets are `startingResources` in `game/data/common/rules.json` (`gold`, `wood`, `aiSpendAbove`, `displayName`, `description`); anything about the rule itself is an inbox note.

### Allies now see through each other's eyes, and an AI ally scouts and gathers near its own home instead of walking across the map; your old recordings refuse to play (sim track, M6-S5, 2026-11-05)

**What was built.** The second half of teams in the rules: **shared vision**. Everything any ally sees, you see: the ground its units and buildings light up, the enemy soldiers in that light, the enemy buildings it finds (they become remembered outlines for you too), the hidden enemy its detector catches, the tower that shot it from a hill. Ground your ally has explored counts as explored for you, so you can build there. Your ally's own units and buildings are always visible to you. A player with no ally sees only through its own eyes, as before. Two AI fixes beside it: an AI ally placed at the mirror start no longer sends its scout to its partner's base and then gives up attacking (it skips the ally's base and sweeps the enemy's half first); and an AI that sees its ally's forest from the first moment no longer marches its woodcutters 300 m across the map to it (it now looks near home first: a new rule, `ai.gatherReach`, 64 m, says a forest or gold mine only counts as "found" within that distance of its Town Hall until its scout is done). Also: when your own Catapult or Cusser kills one of your own or your ally's units, that is a loss for its owner and **nobody's kill** (before, an own friendly-fire kill counted as your kill).

**What you will see or feel.** Set up a 2v2 (Skirmish → Add player twice → Team 1 / 1 / 2 / 2): from the first second you see your AI ally's base, its workers and everything its scout finds; when its army meets the enemy you see the fight. A free-for-all (every slot on None) plays bit for bit as before: the studio replayed five matches of 3,000 ticks against the previous build, identical every tick. **Your recordings made since 2026-10-19 refuse to play** ("another version"): the new rule joined the data fingerprint, as every data change does; recordings from this build on play. Saves from before 2026-10-27 refuse too (the team byte).

**Producer decisions.** (a) **Shared vision is a union, not a copy:** each player's own fog is kept exactly as before (that is what is saved and hashed), and the allies' maps are OR-ed together after each fog update; the alternative, stamping every ally's units into each player's map, cost about 57 % more per fog update in the studio's measurement, the union about 5 %. (b) **64 m for the "look near home" rule:** measured on 20 generated starts, every start's nearest forest is within 21 m of the hall and its second gold mine within 19 m, so 64 m has three times the margin; it is a number in `game/data/common/rules.json` (`ai.gatherReach`). (c) **An ally that is knocked out lends its last sight until the next fog update** (within 4 ticks, a fifth of a second), as a dead unit's sight circle does; not worth a special rule. (d) **Friendly-fire kills are nobody's kill** (the "count only what an enemy destroyed" rule applied to the kill column). To change any of these, write it in the inbox ("no shared vision", "gather reach 96", "count friendly-fire kills").

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1047 (S3):** a start with **no** forest within 64 m of the hall (none of the generated maps has one, but a hand-made map could) gets no wood until its scout has swept the whole map. **BUG-1048 (S3):** an AI whose scout is killed on its very first steps out (an enemy raider at its door at the start) gives up the "near home" rule and, with an ally's vision, can walk its woodcutters across the map after all. Both are decided as one fix (the rule lifts once the scout has looked round home, not when it dies; a resource it can't find near home takes the nearest one it knows): before the hand-made maps, or in the next sim clean-up session. BUG-1049 (S4): small notes. **How to change it:** the number is `ai.gatherReach` in `rules.json`; the rules are an inbox note.

### You can set up a 2v2 from the menu: a Team column per slot, Victory or Defeat for your side, the stats grouped by team (view track, M6-V16, 2026-11-05; landed 2026-11-05-1206)

**In the game since 2026-11-05-1206.** When this work was first merged with the shared-vision change above, one of the view's own test scenes turned red (BUG-1064: the test expected the ally's Town Hall to turn into a remembered outline once the scout walked away, which can't happen any more now that allies always see each other's buildings; the game was fine, the test was wrong). This session dropped that test (what it checked can no longer happen; the code it guarded stays as a safety net), re-ran every test scene on the merged game (76 of 76 green) and landed the branch. Two small things came with it: **the stats screen makes its graph shorter when it has four team labels** so the Back button stays on screen (BUG-1063; see rough edges: a match started from the menu still overflows a little, BUG-1065), and **a setup where every slot is on the same team is refused** (Start greys out with the line "Everyone is on one team: put a player on another team or None"; such a match could never end).

**What was built.** The setup screen's **Team** column (None, Team 1 to Team 4 for each slot; None is the default, so a match set up as before is a free-for-all). The end-of-match banner speaks for **your side**: Victory when the match ends with your team standing (even if you yourself were knocked out earlier and your ally finished it), Defeat only when your whole side is out, Draw when nobody stands; while you are out and your ally fights on there is no banner yet (you watch). The stats screen groups its rows under "Team 1", "Team 2", and the slots with no team under "No team" (found and fixed by QA: without that label the free-for-all seats in a 1v1v2 read as members of the last team). Load Game marks each seat's team, "Malazan Empire (You) (T1)", and the row wraps so a four-seat match shows every mark; saves and recordings made in a team match load and play with their teams. A right-click on an ally's unit, building or minimap dot is a move, not an attack (the sim would have dropped the attack anyway, so the click used to do nothing).

**What you will see or feel.** Skirmish → Add player → Add player → set the four Team lists to Team 1 / Team 1 / Team 2 / Team 2 → Start. You and the AI on Team 1 share vision (the entry above); right-click near your ally's soldiers and your units walk there instead of standing still; when the enemy pair is beaten the banner reads Victory, and Stats shows two groups. Try Team 1 / None / None / None too: a 1v1v1 against you, with "No team" over the three AIs on the stats screen. New words on screen, all from `ui.json`: **"Team"**, **"None"**, **"Team {0}"** (the list items and the stats labels), **"No team"**, and **"{0} (T{1})"** in Load Game.

**Producer decisions.** (a) **Teams 1-4 in the setup** (the rules take up to 8): four slots never need more. (b) **Colours stay per slot, not per team** (team-coloured units are a later polish; say "team colours" in the inbox if you want it sooner). (c) **A setup with every slot on one team is refused at Start** (decided 0805, built 1206): such a match can never end (nobody to beat), so Start stays greyed with a one-line reason; the line sits beside the buttons so the screen keeps its height. The alternative, letting it start as a sandbox, leaves a friend staring at a match that can't finish. (d) The banner's "your side, not you" rule is the one planned on 2026-10-27.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1065 (S3, found 1206):** a teamed four-slot match **started from the menu** (a 2v2, a 1v1v2, four teams) still pushes the Back button about 22 pixels off the bottom of a 1152 × 648 window on the stats screen, because the three AI seats each add an "opened with" line under the table; the button is still clickable and Esc closes the screen. BUG-1063 (the same screen with four team labels, as the tests staged it with human seats) was fixed this session, but the menu's real screen was not covered by it; the fix for 1065 shrinks the graph by the "opened with" lines too, next view session. BUG-1066 (S4): starting a one-team match from the command line (`--team`) is still allowed without a warning (a developer's door, not the menu's), and the Back / Start buttons slide left when the one-team line appears. BUG-1062 (S4) is closed: its three items are all in. **How to change it:** the words are in `game/data/common/ui.json` (`setup.team*`, `match_over.team` / `no_team`, `load.seat_team`); the rules are an inbox note.

### Teams exist in the rules now: allies never attack each other and the last team standing wins; the setup screen shows it next session (sim track, M6-S4, 2026-10-27)

**What was built.** The sim's half of teams (M6 criterion 1's "team", docs/02 "Game flow" 2 and 4). Each seat in a match can carry a team number (none, or 1-8). Two seats on the same team are allies: their units never pick each other as targets, a watch tower never shoots an ally, an attack order aimed at an ally's unit or building is ignored (as one aimed at your own is), an attack-move through an allied army walks on and strikes the enemy behind it. Splash works as for your own side: a Catapult's stone or a Sapper's Cusser hurts an ally's units at the same half damage it does your own, and never an ally's buildings. An ally's sandstorm neither hides its contents from you nor blinds your units inside it, and a hidden (stealthed) unit hides only from enemies, so you see an ally's hidden scout wherever your own units can see. The match ends when every player still in is on one side: in a 2v2, losing one player of a side does not end it; losing both does; a free-for-all ends as before. The AI treats its ally as a non-enemy: it never sends a wave, an attack or a spell at an ally, and an allied army parked beside its hall does not make it call its own army home. Saves (format 3) and recordings (format 7) carry the teams; a recording of a free-for-all is written in the old format 6, byte for byte as before, so the Load Game list keeps reading it.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet. Every match today is still a free-for-all (every seat has no team), and the studio checked that such a match plays bit for bit as it did before this change (five matches replayed 3,000 ticks each against the previous build: identical every tick). The setup screen's **Team** column is the view track's next task (M6-V16); once it lands you'll pick "Team 1" for yourself and one AI, "Team 2" for the others, and the banner will read Victory when your team stands. Your saves from before this session refuse to load ("another version"), as every save format change does; your recordings still play.

**Producer decisions.** (a) **Allies do not share vision yet**: you see an ally's units only where your own units see. Shared vision is the next sim task (M6-S5), built after measuring what a per-team vision layer costs per tick; the design (docs/01, 2026-10-27) is that allies will share what they see. The alternative, no shared vision at all, makes team play blind and was not considered. (b) **A friendly-fire kill is nobody's kill** (BUG-1044 item 1, decided, built in M6-S5): when your Catapult kills one of your own or an ally's units, that unit is a loss for its owner and no kill for anyone (today an own friendly-fire kill still counts as your kill). (c) A free-for-all recording keeps the old format so the game's replay list, which the sim track may not touch, keeps working. To change (a) or (b), write it in the inbox ("no shared vision between allies", "count friendly-fire kills").

**Rough edges.** ~~**BUG-1042 (S3):** with two allies placed at mirror start locations (on the 4-player map: slots 1 and 2 as one team, which is the natural pick), an AI whose scout finds only its ally's base never starts an attack for the whole match: it waits for a known enemy building that never comes.~~ **Fixed in M6-S5 (2026-11-05): the scout skips its ally's base and sweeps the enemy's half first; every seat in the studio's 2v2 soak knows an enemy building and waves.** BUG-1044 (S4): ~~the kill credit above~~ (fixed in M6-S5: nobody's kill) and some test gaps; next sim hardening. The developer command-line tool has no `--teams` flag yet (tests set teams in code). **Update 2026-11-05:** everything "next session" above has landed: shared vision (M6-S5) and the Team column (M6-V16), the two entries just above.

### `main` is clean again and a dozen small sim debts are paid: the save file can't be tricked into grabbing memory, two flaky tests are fixed, the speed budget is gated again (sim track, M5-H4 hardening, 2026-10-26)

**What was built.** A clean-up session, nothing new to play. (1) The nine test rows that were knowingly red on `main` since the AI's reserve landed are green: the four studio-side ones now say exactly what the reserve does (every AI side still standing at 20 minutes has reached Age II **except four named cases**, each with its reason written down, and the wave / defeat totals are checked too; if a sim change ever gets one of the four to Age II, the test prints "take it out"); the five faction-page ones were re-printed by the data track (entry below). (2) **Save files have a hard ceiling on their command queue** (65,536 pending orders, 16× what the game uses). Before, a hand-forged save could claim a queue of a million and make the loader grab ~50 MB before refusing; and a half-made fix inside this session briefly made a real save with a big queue unloadable (BUG-1040, caught by QA, fixed the same session: now a game that can't be loaded can't be created in the first place). Forged projectile and spell-zone counts are bounded too. (3) Two tests that failed once each in a long run are fixed: one really was a Windows file-permission race in the test harness; the other's cause wasn't found, so the test now runs its scene twice and names the first offending moment if it ever fails again. (4) The 4 ms-per-tick speed budget (500 units fighting) is gated again by a short fresh-process test: it reads 3.5-3.9 ms, so there is ~10 % headroom; the "far corner" scan test uses more samples and a tighter bound. (5) Six older nits: a stale AI file with a field set to `null` is refused like every other stale shape; a blocked build step costs one check a think instead of a worker search (AI thinks ~9 % cheaper); the AI no longer reserves gold for a mine its workers found empty; comment and doc fixes.

**What you will notice.** Nothing in play. Saves and replays made by the game are unaffected (it uses 4,096). Only a replay recorded by the developer command-line tool with more than 65,536 units would now refuse to play.

**Producer decisions.** (a) The ceiling is one number shared by the sim, the save and the replay (the alternative, refusing at save time, would leave a running game that can never be saved). (b) Two forged-file refusals changed their reason word from "malformed" to "invalid header", matching the design doc's table; no new error codes (the save API stays frozen). (c) **Worker churn (BUG-1022) stays as it is:** the hardening measured three alternatives on the 27 AI-v-AI matches; the one that recovers the lost 7 % of early gathering delays Age II by 14 s on average, the one that keeps Age II recovers nothing. The table is in docs/03. If you'd rather have the gathering back than 14 s of Age II, write "ship the idle-pass shift" in the inbox.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0960 (S4): one hand-forged save value (a unit's path target) still makes the loader throw instead of refusing; next sim hardening. BUG-1022 / BUG-1026 (S4): tuning notes, above. Not reached this session: BUG-0911, 0889, 0144 (old movement S3s), small doc nits.

### The Load Game list shows the row it picked, a typed count is never lost, and a leftover recording can be deleted (view track, M6-VH4 hardening, 2026-10-26)

**What was built.** Clean-up of the shell. (1) When a save refuses to load, its row stays highlighted **and the list scrolls to it**, even at the bottom of 200 saves, so the Delete button visibly acts on that file. (2) In the skirmish setup, type a number into **Forests** or **Gold mines** and click Start straight away (a touchpad tap, no Enter): the match uses what you typed; an emptied box shows the count that will be used. (3) Ask for 64 gold mines on the smallest map and the generator fits about 60: the match log now says "placed 61 of 64 gold mines asked" and the design doc says why (the map has no more room at the generator's spacing). (4) A recording left in the save folder without its save (you deleted the save outside the game) is listed under Load Game as a replay, so you can watch or delete it. A save made at the very first moment of a match loads with the camera on your base, not the map centre. The pause menu sits on its own opaque panel, so its Save lines no longer draw over the command card at small window sizes. (5) Behind the scenes: the "base under attack" alert bookkeeping could name the wrong alert when 32 alerts piled up in ten seconds (fixed, fuzz-tested); the stats graph's time axis is drawn over the lines (four players at zero used to hide it) and its labels stay at nine or fewer even on a 24-hour span; the smoke test script works on a clone without the sound files (from the second run; the first still fails on the art test's placeholder files).

If you want Violet to read better, that's a colour change in `game/data/common/ui.json` (your taste), not a test change. (c) Two very old nits closed as "won't fix": a case no game path can reach (resource nodes are never re-created mid-match).
