### The AI now saves up for its build order once its army is wave-sized, so it reaches Age II against you; I waived one line of my own brief to keep its waves (sim track, M5-4g, 2026-10-18)

**What was built.** Until now the AI spent every coin on soldiers first, so against a live opponent four of its six openings never
reached Age II in 20 minutes (BUG-0981: it would sit on 1,500 gold and 25 wood, its Age II step unpaid because the wood was always gone).
Now, each time the AI thinks, it looks down its build order for the first due building, research or expansion it can't yet afford and
**keeps that step's cost in reserve**: soldiers are trained only from what is above it, and the workers lean toward the resource the step
is short of (a quarter more of them on gold, or on wood). Houses, the steps earlier in the build order, and its defense are never held
back. **The reserve is kept only once the army is the size of the opening's first wave and the base is not under attack**, so the waves
still come first: the first form (reserve from the first minute) cost a quarter of the AI sides their first wave, and the second (reserve
forever after the first wave) starved the follow-up waves; the shipped one is the third, measured on 27 AI-v-AI matches: sides still
standing at 20:00 without Age II **23 of 41 → 4 of 49**, Malazan waves **79 → 81**, defeats Malazan / Whirlwind **8 / 5 → 5 / 0**.

**What you will see or feel.** A Normal or Hard opponent that survives your early raids now **gets to Age II** (its mages, Zealots,
rams and Age II upgrades show up in the second half of a match instead of almost never), and it still attacks you in waves about as
often as before. Nothing changes in the first five minutes. Its base will sometimes sit on a few hundred gold for a minute or two while
it saves up; that is the reserve. **Not changed:** the "Fast Age II" and "Crossbow push" openings still fall to the Whirlwind's Raider
rush without ever attacking on most seeds (BUG-1010): the builder built a "defend, then counter-attack" rule, and 0 of 6 test matches
waved under it, so it was taken out again; it comes back once the data track has looked at those openings' wave sizes.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) **I waived one line of my brief:** it asked that *every* AI side alive at 20:00 reach Age
II. Nine forms of the rule were measured on the same 27 matches and none keeps both every Age II and every wave (every think the AI saves
is a think it doesn't train); I kept the form that keeps the waves. The four sides that miss Age II never had it before this change
either (one is under its wave size all match, so its reserve never engages; three know no gold mine by then). (2) **The army counts its
soldiers out on a wave too** when it judges "wave-sized" (BUG-1026): so while a wave is marching the base keeps saving, and once the
wave dies it rebuilds before saving again. Counting only the soldiers at home is a measured alternative that trades Age II for waves
again; kept as a tuning note. (3) The reserve is a per-think scratch value, not stored: **your saves still load** (format unchanged).
(4) Two new numbers live in `game/data/common/rules.json` (`ai.reserveShift` 0.25, `ai.reserveArmyShare` 1: 0 would reserve from the
first minute), so **recordings made before 2026-10-19 refuse to play** (the data fingerprint moved).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1027 (S2, housekeeping, not the game):** the faction pages' measured spending cells and five of the studio's own
pinned tests are now out of date, and four stress tests were written to the line I waived: nine test rows are red on `main` until the next
session's first items (the data track's re-print, the sim's restatement). **BUG-1022 (S4):** the workers switch between gold and wood
about three times as often as before (4 a minute), which costs the AI about 7 % of its gathering in the first ten minutes (even by 20:00);
a "stick with the choice until the step is paid" rule is the fix, next sim hardening. **BUG-1023 (S4):** an expansion can be reserved for a
mine the workers found empty. **BUG-1026 (S4):** on Easy, one measured match went from 5 waves alive to 2 waves and a defeat; on Hard,
one Whirlwind match sends no wave where it sent one: the tuning pass's cases. **How to change it:** edit the two numbers in `rules.json`
(`reserveArmyShare` 0.5 = save up once the army is half a wave), or an inbox note ("let the AI save up from the start", "never hold more
than 300 gold", "count only the soldiers at home").

### The skirmish setup has a game speed and the map's forests and gold mines; a refused load keeps its row; a loaded match runs at Normal speed (view track, M6-V15, 2026-10-18)

**What was built.** In **Skirmish setup**: a **Game speed** list (Slow 0.75×, Normal 1×, Fast 1.5×; Normal by default) beside the map
size, and a **Forests** and a **Gold mines** count (12 and 8 by default; at least one forest and two mines per player so every base keeps
its start forest and start mines; at most 64 each; adding a player raises a count that is now under the floor). The counts are part of
the map, so a save or a replay of that match rebuilds the same map. The two Save / Load rough edges from last session are closed: after
"This save is damaged" the **damaged file's own row stays highlighted**, so Delete removes it and not your newest save (BUG-1000); and a
**loaded match always runs at Normal speed** (BUG-1001, settled rather than "restored": the save holds no speed, and the speed you pick in
the setup belongs to the match you start with it). Saving a match against the AI is now proven through the real screen too (the studio
saved the menu's match against a Normal AI at five different moments, loaded each and ran it beside the unsaved copy: identical).

**What you will see or feel.** Pick **Fast** for a quicker match or **Slow** to learn; set **Forests 20 / Gold mines 16** for a richer map
or 2 / 4 for a poor one (the floor follows your player count). Load a save and it runs at Normal whatever you picked. **Try:** Skirmish →
Forests 6, Gold mines 4, Start; Esc → Save; Load Game → Load: the same sparse map comes back.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) **A loaded match runs at Normal speed** (documented) rather than carrying the speed in the
save (the save format is frozen this milestone) or using the setup's current pick (surprising if you changed it since). (2) **The counts
clamp silently** to the floor and the cap (typing 1 gives you the floor, 1000 gives 64).

**Rough edges.** **BUG-1030 (S3):** if the damaged save is far down a long list, its row is highlighted but off-screen (the list shows its
top); Delete still removes the right file, but you can't see it: scroll down to check, fixed next view session. **BUG-1031 (S3):** a count
*typed* into Forests / Gold mines without pressing Enter is lost if you tap Start very quickly (a touchpad tap); press Enter or use the
arrows until the next view session fixes it. **BUG-1032 (S4):** 64 gold mines on the smallest (128) map places 60-62 without saying so.
**How to change it:** the texts are `setup.speed*`, `setup.forests`, `setup.mines` in `game/data/common/ui.json`; the defaults are in the
game's launch options; an inbox note for the rest ("keep the speed in the save", "offer Very fast 2×", "a starting-resources choice":
that one needs a sim option first, Requests 43).

### You can save a match and load it later: Esc → Save, then Main menu → Load Game → Load (view track, M6-V14, 2026-10-18)

**What was built.** The Save / Load screen on top of the save format the rules side finished this session (the next entry). **Try it:**
start a skirmish against the AI, play a few minutes, press **Esc** and click **Save**: the pause menu says "Saved at 3:12" (the match
clock). Quit to menu (or keep playing and save again later: every save is a new file). From the main menu open **Load Game**: your saves
and your recorded replays sit in one list, newest first, each row with the date, the seed, the players, the match time it was made at and a
**Save** or **Replay** tag. Pick a save and click **Load** (or double-click it): the match comes back at that exact moment, your base in
view, nothing selected, fog and minimap as they were, the AI carrying on with the plan it had, and continues exactly as it would have
without the save (the studio proved that by running a loaded copy beside an unsaved one for 1,000 ticks with the match fingerprint equal
every tick, and the rules side for 2,000-6,000 ticks on 20 kinds of moment). **Delete** removes a save (and the recording that was written
beside it). A damaged or foreign file is refused with a plain reason ("This save is damaged and can't be read.", "This save was made with
different game data…") and never crashes the game; files that can't be read at all are still listed so you can delete them. The save files
live in `%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\RtsGame\saves\` (about 4 MB each); the `--load <path>` flag starts the game straight into one.

**What you will see or feel.** A loaded match **is not recorded**: the pause menu says "A loaded match is not recorded: no replay is kept
from here on." (a recording has to start with the match; the recording up to the moment you saved is written beside the save file and plays
from Load Game → Watch as usual). Saves are never pruned; replays still keep the newest 20.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) **Saves and replays share one list** (one place to look, the tag tells them apart) rather than
two screens. (2) **A loaded match is not recorded** rather than stitching the two recordings together (a stitched replay would need the
save inside it; the rules side's save holds no replay, decision of 2026-10-18-0516). (3) **The Save button is never greyed:** it asks the rules
side and shows the reason if refused, so it worked for AI matches the moment slice 2 landed. (4) The builder added a developer-only launch
flag (`--ai <slot> human`, so a test match can have two human seats) that was not in the brief; harmless, documented, kept.

**Rough edges.** ~~**BUG-1000 (S3):** after a refused Load the list jumps its highlight to the newest row, so pressing Delete right after
"This save is damaged" would delete the *newest* save, not the damaged one. Check the highlighted row before you press Delete; fixed in the
view's next task.~~ **Fixed (M6-V15, 2026-10-18):** the refused file's row stays highlighted under its reason, so Delete removes that file
(one leftover, BUG-1030: if that row is far down a long list, the list shows its top and the highlighted row is off-screen; fixed next view
session). ~~**BUG-1001 (S3):** a loaded match always runs at normal speed even if you set up the match at Fast (the speed isn't in the
save); the view's next task makes a load use the speed the skirmish setup currently shows and says so in the docs.~~ **Settled (M6-V15):** a
loaded match runs at Normal speed, always, and the docs say so (the save holds no speed; the setup's speed belongs to the match it started;
the setup now has a Game speed list, see the M6-V15 entry above). **BUG-1002 (S4):** a save
made before the first tick loads with the camera on the map centre; the pause menu's two save lines can overlap the command card; a stray
recording file left in the save folder can't be deleted from the game. **How to change it:** the texts are `save.*`, `pause.save` and
`load.*` in `game/data/common/ui.json`; the folder is `user://saves`; an inbox note for anything else ("saves should also keep the game
speed", "one Save slot that overwrites", "autosave every 5 minutes").

### Saving a match against the AI now works too: the AI's memory is in the save (sim track, M6-S3 "save slice 2", 2026-10-18)

**What was built.** The second half of the rules side's save: each AI opponent's memory goes into the save file, whole: which opening it
chose, how far it is through its build order, every order it has pending, its retry marks, scout, wave, retreat and defense bookkeeping,
its recent spells, and the exact state of its dice. On load the AI seat is rebuilt as a new match builds it, its chosen opening checked
against the one the seed gives (a file edited to say otherwise is refused as damaged), and its memory written back over it. The save file
format is stamped **version 2** (nothing shipped a version-1 file: the human-only slice was never behind a button).

**What you will see or feel.** With the entry above: a loaded match's AI **continues its plan** rather than starting a new one; a wave
that was marching stays on its way, a building it was placing still goes up where it meant to, a spell it had ready is still ready. The
studio compared the orders the loaded AI sends with the orders the never-saved AI sends, tick by tick, at 17 kinds of moment (mid-wave,
retreating, pulling home for a defense, waiting on a blocked site, a spell just cast) and through a chain of 24 reloads: identical every time.
A save of the menu's match against a Normal AI is about 4.1 MB and takes about 30 ms to write and 60 ms to read.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) **Version 2 with no reader for version 1** (nothing to migrate). (2) **The AI's scratch
is stored too** rather than proving which parts are rewritten before being read (cheaper to store a few KB than to prove it; the file grows
by tens of KB per AI seat). (3) The 1.4 GB forged-file problem from last session (BUG-0960 item 1) is closed by a size check before any
memory is allocated: a hand-forged file claiming a million units is now refused in a fifth of a millisecond.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-0990 (S4):** the new size check counts units, buildings, resources and map cells but not pending commands,
projectiles or spell zones, so a hand-forged file claiming a million of those still makes the loader take up to 180 MB before refusing it,
and one claiming a huge command queue loads with that queue size; only a file edited by hand with its checksum recomputed gets here; the
next sim hardening. BUG-0960 items 2-3 stay open (documented limits of a checksum-valid forgery). **How to change it:** an inbox note.

### "Fast Age II" keeps its 18-pop first wave: measured, and the page now says it can fall to a rush without attacking (data track, D-H6, 2026-10-18)

**What was decided.** Last session's BUG-0982: the Malazan "Fast Age II" opening was beaten by the Whirlwind "Raider rush" on seed 8
without ever attacking. The data track measured it instead of guessing: the pair was played 20 minutes at a first-wave threshold of 18
(today's), 16 and 14 army pop on seeds 7, 8 and 14 (QA added 18 and 23). **Result:** on every seed but 7 the Malazan army never grows past
8-12 pop while it defends against the raids, so a lower threshold sends no wave either; it only makes seed 7 attack earlier (8:42 → 7:54).
Age II is never delayed. So **the number stays at 18**, the player-facing description ("The first wave waits for 18 army pop.") stays, and
`docs/factions/malazan.md` says in plain words that this greedy opening can die to a rush without attacking, with the full table. **No data
changed, your recordings still play.**

**What changed for you to review:** nothing in the game's numbers or texts. Two reporting improvements: the studio's opening-pairs report now
prints how long each unpaid build step has been waiting and the banks (so BUG-0981's "the AI never saves up for Age II" pattern is visible:
11 of 54 sides show it), and every Malazan × Whirlwind pairing is now played on three seeds instead of two.

**The real finding (BUG-1010, S3, rules side).** Against the Raider rush, "Fast Age II" sends no wave on 4 of 5 seeds and "Crossbow push"
on 2 of 5: a Normal Whirlwind AI that rolls the raider rush beats two of the three Malazan openings without a fight most of the time. No
threshold fixes it; the lever is a rule: "send what you have when the base is being lost" (or defend, then counter-attack). Planned with the
sim's M5-4g (the Age II reserve), the next sim task. **How to change it:** an inbox note ("Fast Age II should wave at 14 anyway", "give the
Malazan openings a second Barracks early") makes it a data task; otherwise the rules-side fix comes first and the pages are re-measured after.

### Nothing you can click yet, but the game can now save a match and bring it back exactly (sim track, M6-S2 "save slice 1", 2026-10-18)

**What was built.** The rules side of saving: a save file format and two doors into the simulation, "write this match to a file" and
"read a file back into a running match". A save holds everything: every unit and building with its orders and queues, every tree and
mine, the arrows in flight, the sandstorms and burning ground, what each side has explored and remembers, the pathfinding caches, the dice
(every random stream's exact state), the pending orders, the match stats and the "match over" latch. Loading rebuilds the match on the
stored map without re-rolling anything.

**What you will see or feel.** Nothing yet: the **Save** button in the pause menu and **Load Game → saves** arrive next session (the
view track builds the screen against this format). When they do, a loaded match continues *exactly* as the unsaved one would have: the
studio proved it by saving at 13 different moments (mid-brawl, mid-spell, a building half built, a side already knocked out, …), loading,
and running both copies on for 2,000 more ticks (QA: 6,000, and a chain of 24 reloads) with the match fingerprint equal every tick. A damaged
or edited file is refused with a reason, never a crash (QA tried 621,000 corrupted files). A save of the menu's match is about 3.9 MB and
takes about 25 ms to write and 46 ms to read.

**Limits this session (by design).** Only matches whose seats are all human can be saved so far: a match against an AI opponent is
refused with "AI seats unsupported" until **slice 2, next session**, stores the AI's memory (its build-order progress, its chosen opening,
its dice). So the first time you can actually save a skirmish against the AI is after the next session. **Update 2026-10-18-1236:** slice 2
landed (the entry above this one): matches against the AI save and load too, and the Save / Load buttons are in the game.

**Producer decisions (owner may revisit).** (1) **Pathfinding caches are stored, not recomputed**, as decided on 2026-10-07; to keep the
file small the directions are stored and the distances are recomputed only where the maths proves them identical, with the raw numbers
written for any field that breaks the rule (3.9 MB instead of about 12 MB; the round-trip tests compare every number). (2) **Humans first,
AI second:** the format and every store landed this session, the AI's memory next session, so the view's screen can be built against a
frozen format in parallel. (3) **The recording of the match so far is not inside the save**; the Save screen will write it beside the save
file. (4) Slice 2 will stamp the format **version 2** (nothing has shipped a version-1 save).

**Rough edges.** BUG-0960 (S4, not blocking): a hand-forged file claiming a million units makes the loader grab 1.4 GB of memory before
refusing it (a cheap check lands with slice 2); a few of the 47,714 forged files that passed the checksum then misbehaved on the next tick
(documented: a checksum-valid forgery is trusted). **How to change it:** an inbox note (e.g. "saves must also work mid-tick" or "compress
the save files").

### The end-of-match screen now says which opening the AI played; a raid that reaches your buildings now reads "base under attack"; the stuck test scene is fixed (view track, M6-V13, 2026-10-18)

**What you will see.** (1) On the **Victory / Defeat stats screen**, between the table and the army graph, one line per AI opponent in
its colour: "**Malazan Empire opened with Crossbow push**" (the faction's name and the opening's name from the data; hover the line for
the opening's description). You get no line (you chose your own plan). Watching a replay shows the same lines. (2) **Attack alerts:** when
a raid hits your soldiers first and then your Town Hall, the text now changes from "Your units are under attack" to "**Your base is
under attack**" (before, the first hit decided the wording for 10 s); no second alarm, no second minimap ping, it is the same alert.
(3) A studio test scene (`QaM6V11Test`) that waited for the AIs to finish off an idle player, and had gone red since the AI stopped
hunting last workers, now stages that defeat itself; the whole scene loop is green again (69 / 69). The AI's own gap (it never hunts an
idle player's last five workers) is still open for the sim's M5-4d.

**Producer / dev decisions.** The line reads "<faction> opened with <opening>" so two AIs of one faction tell apart by their colour swatch;
a human seat shows nothing rather than an "opened with your own plan" filler. For a watched replay (where every seat plays as a human) the
view works out the AI's pick from the match seed with the same dice roll the sim makes, so the line is right without storing it.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0970 (S4, not blocking): the "upgrade to base" bookkeeping can name the wrong alert when 32 alerts pile up within 10 s
(the ring is full); fixed at the next view hardening. **How to change it:** the wording is `match_over.opening` in `game/data/common/ui.json`
(`"{0} opened with {1}"`); the alert texts are `alert.base_under_attack` / `alert.units_under_attack`.

### The AI can now carry several named openings per faction and picks one at the start of each match; your old recordings refuse to play (sim track, M5-8a, 2026-10-17)

### The AI can now carry several named openings per faction and picks one at the start of each match; your old recordings refuse to play (sim track, M5-8a, 2026-10-17)

**What was built.** Your D14 b request, the machinery half. Each faction's AI data file (`game/data/factions/<id>/ai.json`) now holds a
list of **openings**, one to eight, each with its own build order, army mix and "attack when I have this much army" thresholds, plus a
name and a one-line description the game can show. At the start of a match **an Easy AI always plays the first opening** (a learner meets
the same game every time); **a Normal or Hard AI picks one at random from the match seed**, so the same seed always gives the same pick
(a replay or a save reproduces it) and a different seed can open differently. Today both files hold exactly one opening, "Standard"
(the build order you have been playing against, unchanged step for step), so **nothing plays differently yet**: the data track writes
the real openings next session (D21: three per faction, e.g. a standard build, an early rush, a fast Age II) and you get their names and
descriptions in a review table. Folded in: a small AI fix (BUG-0910): a building the AI was waiting to unlock (a Corral waiting on its
Barracks) now goes up 1-2 thinks after the requirement is met, not 1-5 (2.5-10 s on Easy).

**What you will see.** Nothing new until D21 lands; after it, two Normal matches against the same faction on different seeds can open
with different builds. **Recordings you made before this session refuse to play** (Main menu → Load Game → Watch stops with a data
mismatch): the data fingerprint covers the file's new shape and the openings' names. New recordings are fine; D21 moves it once more.

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (1) **Normal and Hard pick the same opening on the same seed** (one draw from the AI's own
random stream, the first and only draw it makes): simplest, reproducible, and the difficulty's knobs still differ; the alternative
(a separate draw per difficulty) buys nothing a player would notice. (2) **The pick is not part of the game's fingerprint** (AI state,
like its blackboard): a replay never runs the AI, and hashing it would invalidate replays for no gain; the save format stores it.
(3) **Names and descriptions live in the data file**, not in code, so a later "the AI opened with Crossbow push" line on the stats
screen (the view's next task) reads them from there and the data track can reword them.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0940 (S4): a stale AI file that writes the old top-level `buildOrder` as `null` loads silently instead of being
refused (every other stale shape is refused); next sim clean-up. BUG-0941 (S4): the AI fix costs about 0.03 ms on its slowest think
(0.17 → 0.20 ms; the gate is 1 ms); next sim clean-up.

**How to change it.** The openings are data: `game/data/factions/<id>/ai.json` `openings[]` (D21 fills them; an inbox note after the
review table changes any of them). To make Easy pick at random too, or Hard pick from a different draw, write it in the inbox.

### The game has real sounds, and your base warns you when it is attacked (view track, M6-V12, 2026-10-17)

**What was built.** (a) **Real sound effects** cut from your Sonniss GDC 2026 bundle: 16 short clips for 12 events: select, order,
refused, a melee blow (three variants in turn), a shot loosed, a unit's death (two), a building placed, a building finished, a building
razed, a unit or tech ready (two), a spell, and the alarm. Each clip is listed in `tools/audio/sfx-manifest.json` (which Sonniss file,
where it was cut, how long) and rebuilt by `tools/audio/trim-wav.ps1`; every source pack has a row in docs/04's licensing log (the
bundle's licence: royalty-free, no attribution). **No raw pack or uncut file is in the repo.** (b) **Fight sounds only for what you
see:** blows, shots, deaths, razing and spells play only when they happen on your screen and in your sight, at most four starting in
any tenth of a second (a 200 v 200 brawl is a texture, not a wall). Your own cues (select, order, refused, building placed / finished,
ready, the alarm) always play and are never cut short by a busy fight. (c) **Attack alerts:** when one of your buildings or units loses
hit points, at most once per 30 m per 10 s of game time: if it is off screen, "Your base is under attack" (a building) or "Your units
are under attack" (a unit) shows for 4 s at the top centre, a red ring pulses on the minimap for 3 s and the alarm sounds; if it is on
screen, only the ring and the alarm. **Space** jumps the camera to the last alert (Space is now a fixed key, like Esc). A watched
replay shows the same alerts at the same moments. (d) **A music hook:** any `.ogg` dropped in `game/assets/audio/music/` plays on a
loop (in name order) on the Music bus, whose volume is the Settings slider; none ships (your download). (e) A red studio test scene
(BUG-0920) fixed. (f) The game still boots and plays with the fallback tones on a machine that cloned the repo without the sound files
(one warning per event).

**What you will see and hear.** Select a worker: a click. Right-click: a short accept. Send Heavy Infantry into Raiders: metal and body
blows, yells when units die; pull the camera away and the brawl goes silent. Place a Billet: a wooden knock; when it finishes, wooden
pieces settle. Train a worker: a kalimba note. Let Raiders hit your hall while you look elsewhere: the alarm, the text, the minimap
ring; press Space and you are there. **Nobody in the studio can hear the clips: the choice of sounds is yours to judge** (the item under
"Waiting on you" says how to tell us which to re-cut).

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (1) The on-screen rule and the four-per-100-ms cap (the alternative, every fight on the map
audible, is noise in a 4-player match). (2) The alert rule's 30 m / 10 s and the text only when the fight is off screen (on screen you
can see it; the ring and the alarm still tell you). (3) Space as the jump key (StarCraft's convention; it was free). (4) Music stays a hook:
no placeholder track was picked for you. (5) No clip is named in code: the game finds `assets/audio/sfx/<category>/<event>_<n>.wav`, so
re-cutting or adding a variant is a manifest row + the script, no code.

**Rough edges, with when they're fixed.** BUG-0954 item 1 (S4): a raid that hits a worker beside your hall a moment before the hall reads
"Your units are under attack" while the hall burns (the first hit fixes the wording); the view's next session. BUG-0955 (S3): on a
machine that cloned the repo without the sound files, the studio's smoke gate still goes red (Godot's importer complains about the
missing files every run) although the game runs fine there; a studio tooling quirk, next view clean-up. BUG-0953 (S3): one studio test
scene is red because the AI never finishes off an idle player's last workers (the sim's M5-4d gap; the view re-stages the scene next
session).

**How to change it.** A sound: an inbox note naming the event and what is wrong (or a Sonniss file you prefer: the manifest takes a
file, a start and a length). The alert text: `game/data/common/ui.json` `alert.*`. The rules (30 m, 10 s, 4 per 100 ms, 4 s of text):
constants in `AttackAlerts` / `Sfx` / `AlertHud`, an inbox note moves them (or into `rules.json` if you want to tune them yourself).

### Sim clean-up: workers no longer stand idle beside a crowded mine, spammed orders behind a long line of your own archers arrive, the speed gates fit this PC, and "spawn order" is settled as a known limit (sim track, M5-H3 hardening, 2026-10-17)

**What was fixed (9 bugs closed, 4 left for the next clean-up).** (a) **Workers at a crowded mine or tree (BUG-0790):** a worker that
arrived at a packed mine face on a diagonal was sent to queue behind the others even when a spot in reach right beside it was free, and
could stand there doing nothing for 3-4 seconds at a time. Now the four corner spots of a mine or tree count as places to stand, and a
worker whose own spot has room stays there. Over 32 test maps and 640 crowded set-ups, workers wedged out of reach went from 9 cases
to 0. (b) **Spammed Moves behind your own line (BUG-0887):** right-clicking every few ticks between two points behind a row of 24-32 of
your own shooting Crossbowmen made the walker swing along the row for 45 s and never arrive; it now arrives within ~10 s with at most
a few turns. (c) **A line against a cliff (BUG-0888):** a walker behind the cliff end of a long line went round the far end and then gave
up on the way back; it now gets there. (d) **The AI stopped wasting its thinking time (BUG-0791):** when the AI could afford a building
but had no free worker, or had just failed to find a site, it searched the whole base area again every think; in a crowded late game
that was most of its think time (0.9 of 0.9 ms). It now skips the search when no worker is free and waits five thinks after a failed
site search. (e) **The speed gates (BUG-0764, a Producer decision, see below).** (f) Three test-quality fixes (a test that never took its
order, two missing test rows), BUG-0886 / BUG-0850.

**What you will see.** Send 40 workers to a mine open on one side: they settle into reach faster and fewer stand around behind the
others; in the recorded seed-21 match the wood count at the end goes from 235 to 895 because the wood gatherers no longer wedge at the
tree corners (**so gathering is noticeably better at crowded nodes**; the faction pages' AI spending paragraphs were re-printed, below).
Plant 32 Crossbowmen in a row, put a soldier behind them and spam right-clicks past the row: he walks round the end and arrives.

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (1) **The speed gates were re-set to this PC's slow clock.** Since 2026-10-15, 16 benchmark
rows failed on every branch alike. The cause is the PC, not the game: it runs a short burst fast and slows to about 0.6× within a few
seconds of sustained load, and the long benchmark run sees the slow figure. Each gate was re-measured four times on an idle machine and
set to the measured figure plus at most 25 %, with the old value, the readings and the date in a comment next to it (docs/03 "Re-baselined
for this PC"). Trade-off: a gate now says "not 25 % worse than this PC's slow figure", so **the 4 ms-per-tick design budget for 500 units
is not checked by any gate on this PC** (BUG-0912); the studio shows every feature's cost by a paired before / after measurement
instead. If the PC stops slowing down (power plan, thermals: "Waiting on you" item 2), the gates come back down. (2) **"Spawn order" is a
documented known limit, not a bug (BUG-0885 with BUG-0046 closed).** The game's promise is "same seed + same orders = same match"; it never
promised that spawning the same units in another order gives the same crowd. Making it so would re-roll every crowd outcome for an
independence nothing relies on. Rules that read a set of units must still not depend on the order they visit them in, and every movement
change ships a same-order determinism twin (docs/03 "Determinism"). (3) The AI's five-think wait after a failed site search is a fixed
engine constant, not a data knob (an inbox note moves it to `rules.json` if you'd rather tune it).

**Rough edges, with when they're fixed.** BUG-0910 (S3): the five-think wait also delays a building the AI was waiting to unlock (a Corral
waiting on its Barracks) by up to 2.5-10 s depending on difficulty; a few lines, folded into the sim's next task. BUG-0912 (S3): one gate
(the "far-corner scan") was set from a single high reading; the next sim clean-up gives it more samples. BUG-0911 (S3, older than this
work): spammed Moves behind a **short** line of 10 at 30-45° still swing; next clean-up. BUG-0889 (S3): a soldier ordered onto an enemy
hall who ends up 2 cm out of reach, or queued behind his own archers on that hall, keeps "Moving" instead of striking or giving up; next
clean-up. BUG-0914 (S4): one memory-check test failed once in a full run and passed every time since; watched. **Replays:** the worker
change moves where workers stand from tick 19 of any match with gathering, so **recordings you made before today refuse to play**
(Main menu → Load Game → Watch stops with a mismatch); new recordings are fine.

### Your infantry now walk round your own crossbow line instead of standing stuck behind it, and they keep their target while they do; the faction pages' balance tables move with it (sim track, M5-P2 "pathing slice 2", 2026-10-17)

**What was built.** The second half of your playtest note 5 ("infantry behind crossbowmen get stuck instead of going around them").
A soldier whose way is blocked by its own side's standing fighters (units that are shooting or casting: they never get pushed) now
walks round the **nearer end** of that line, turning up to 135° off its course, and once it has picked a side it keeps it. While it
walks round friends who are fighting the same enemy it **does not give the enemy up** (before, it gave up after 2 s and stood idle). A
plain right-click Move through your own line does the same, so a group sent past its archers gets there. Two limits on purpose: a
block of more than 32 touching fighters is an army's front, not a line (the back ranks queue behind it as before), and **enemy** lines
are never walked round (the old rule that an enemy wall holds is untouched). One fix inside the same work: an attack order on a
target nobody can reach (a unit up a sealed cliff, a hall ringed by trees) is now given up instead of pacing below it forever.

**What you will see.** Plant 10 Crossbowmen in a row shooting an enemy Town Hall, put 10 Heavy Infantry behind them and order them to
attack the hall: 8 of 10 strike within 10 s (before: 0; they stood behind the row and gave up). Whirlwind Raiders behind Desert
Archers: 10 of 10. Attack-move past the row, or an enemy unit walking up behind your line: 9-10 of 10 reach it, nobody gives up.
Move 10 infantry to a point beyond your crossbow row: 9 of 10 arrive. In a melee between two armies the back ranks walk round their
own front rank's ends instead of pressing behind it, so **brawls between melee groups are quicker and more one-sided** (one
attack-move in a 40 v 40 test brawl now deals 46 % more damage than before).

**Balance tables moved (for your review; the data track re-prints the pages).** The counter-triangle fights on the faction pages
(Malazan vs Whirlwind pairs, both seats) were re-measured. **Every winner is unchanged.** The margins:

| Fight | Winner keeps (cost), old → new | Time to last death, old → new |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heavy Infantry v Horse Raider (seat 0 / 1) | 94 / 88 % → **100 / 100 %** | 23.1 / 20.5 s → 17.9 / 16.3 s |
| Raider v Wickan Lancer | 100 / 95 % → 95 / 95 % | 16.6 / 18.3 s → 15.6 / 15.9 s |
| Wickan Lancer v Desert Archer | 70 / 80 % → 80 / 80 % | 25.1 / 22.0 s → 15.9 / 16.4 s |
| Horse Raider v Crossbowman | 69 / 77 % → **92 / 85 %** | 20.9 / 18.2 s → 14.8 / 14.6 s |
| Crossbowman v Priest of the Whirlwind | 87 / 67 % → 87 / 60 % | 11.6 / 11.9 s → 13.4 / 13.6 s |
| Desert Archer v Cadre Mage | 89 / 72 % → 89 / 89 % | 11.4 / 13.0 s → 9.6 / 11.4 s |

Reading it: melee winners now win faster and lose fewer (they stop queueing behind their own front); the two ranged-v-caster rows move
a little the other way. Every row was already above the 40-65 % target band (a Producer default from D6; D13 / D18 found no lever of
the line unit's own that reaches it), and this pushes the melee rows further from it. If you want the margins pulled back toward the
band, that is a data task (unit numbers), not a pathing one: say so in the inbox. The AI's spending paragraphs moved by 1-4 s (the
idle base falls at 505 s, not 509 s). No data file changed.

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (a) The walk round the line is remembered for a while, so a unit keeps the side it took
and doesn't swing between the two ends (that memory is part of the game's fingerprint). (b) A line of 11 or more is remembered; round
a line of 10 or fewer the simple rule alone does the job (the memory made units converging on a melee give up more). (c) The
determinism proof uses one walker in nine layouts (bit-equal whichever order the row was spawned in); the full 10 v 10 scene was never
spawn-order free, even before this change (BUG-0885, to be looked at in the sim's clean-up).

**Replays.** The rule changes where units walk, and the "fingerprint" grew a word for a unit that has walked round its line, so **a
replay recorded before today may refuse to play** (Main menu → Load Game → Watch stops with a mismatch) wherever a melee unit flanked
its own line. New recordings are fine. Nothing to do unless you want an old one kept: say so and the studio can keep it with the old
build.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0887 (S3): a Move re-issued every 2-3 ticks (click spam) to two points 2 m apart behind a line of 24-32 swings for
ever (the old behaviour never arrived either). BUG-0888 (S3): behind a long line that ends against a cliff, the walker goes round the
open end and gives its Move up 14 m short on the way back. BUG-0889 (S3, older than this change): a Crossbowman ordered onto a hall
behind its own Crossbowmen, or a Heavy Infantry a hair out of reach at a corner, keeps walking and never strikes. BUG-0885 (S3, above).
BUG-0886 (S3): one of the dev's regression tests doesn't test what it says (QA's own does). All in the sim's next clean-up (M5-H3,
next session). The 8-of-10 result in the Heavy Infantry scene sits exactly on its bound: the last two strike late on the hall's far
faces, which is the next pathing slice ("far faces first").

**How to change it.** The turn limit, the memory and the 32-unit line bound are movement constants in code (`MovementConstants`,
documented in docs/03 "Implementation (pathing slice 2)"); an inbox note changes any of them. Balance: an inbox note to the data track.

### The game counts your match stats now: gathered, trained, kills and losses by kind, buildings built and lost, when each tech finished, and your army's value every ten seconds (sim track, M6-S1, 2026-10-17)

**What was built.** Per player, the simulation keeps: gold and wood **gathered** (counted when a worker drops its load off, so refunds and
the starting purse don't count); **units trained** (finished from a production queue; summoned creatures and the start workers don't
count); **kills and losses split** into units and buildings (they add up exactly to the kill and loss counts you already see); **buildings
built** (a construction finished; the Town Hall you start with doesn't count) and **lost**; the moment each tech finished (so "time to
Age II" is one read); and a sample of the **army's value** (the gold + wood cost of every live non-worker unit) every 10 seconds, kept for
2 h 50 min of match, for the graph.

**What you will see.** Nothing yet: this task is the bookkeeping. The view's next task puts the columns and the army-value graph on the
Victory / Defeat stats screen (and the pause menu's Stats), per docs/02 "Game flow" 5. Your recorded replays still play.

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (a) **None of it is part of the game's fingerprint** (the hash that replays are checked
against): it decides nothing in the match, so hashing it would only make every old recording refuse to play. (b) The 10-second cadence is
a program setting, not a line in `rules.json`, for the same reason (a data change expires your recordings; this one didn't). (c)
**Summoned creatures count in the army value** while they live, at their type's cost (the graph shows what stands on the field, not what
was paid). The alternative, counting only paid units, is one line if you prefer it.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-0850** (S4): the developer's own tests missed two corner cases (a cancelled site's gold refund; a summon from a
real spell cast); the QA inspector's tests cover both and the game behaves right; the dev's rows get patched in the sim's next clean-up.
A replay watched with a different sample cadence would show a differently spaced graph (the cadence isn't stored in the recording; a later
format can add it).

**How to change it.** Inbox: "count only trained units in army value", "sample every 5 s", or anything about which columns you want.

### The AI now answers a raid with just what it is worth: one Raider pulls two defenders while its attack goes on; gathering is about 20 % quicker (sim track, M5-4f, 2026-10-16)

**What was built.** Your 2026-10-14 request ("a small raid must not recall the whole wave"), plus three small things from the same
review:

1. **The sized defense.** When enemies show up near the AI's Town Hall, it adds up what they cost (gold + wood of every attacker it can
   see) and sends home defenders worth **1.5× that, at least 150** (about two line units). It takes them from the units already at home
   first (the nearest to the trouble), then from its attack wave, soldier by soldier from the ones nearest home, **as long as the wave stays
   big enough to keep attacking** (the size it set out with). The **whole wave** only turns round when the raid is worth more than
   everything else it could send, or when its **Town Hall is being hit and is under half hp**. A hit by something it can't see (a catapult
   in the fog) gets the minimum answer. The defenders stay assigned while the raid lasts, and a fallen one is replaced.
2. **Gathering is quicker**: gold 0.7 → **0.85** a second per worker, wood 0.6 → **0.75** (your playtest note 3, "gathering felt slow";
   about +20 %: five workers bring 200 gold in roughly 47 s instead of 57).
3. **No wasted house**: the AI skips a house in its build order once its population cap is already at the hard maximum (your D15 option C).
4. **Spell aim**: the AI's mage aims at the enemy group **nearest to it** instead of at the average position of every enemy in reach,
   which used to fall between two groups and hit neither.

**What you will see.** Send one Raider into the AI's base: two or three of its soldiers turn to meet it and its army keeps marching on
you (before, the whole army came home for one Raider). Send eight: its home guard plus the nearest part of the wave come back, the rest
press on. Send twelve, or get its Town Hall under half hp: everything comes home, and its next wave waits out the usual cooldown. Your own
workers fill the resource bar visibly faster from the first minute. The AI's Easy / Normal / Hard play all use the same defense numbers.

**Producer decisions (yours to revisit).** (a) The three numbers **1.5 / 150 / 0.5** are the ones from my 2026-10-14 design; they live in
`game/data/common/rules.json` under `ai` (`defendRatio`, `defendMinValue`, `recallHallHp`) and any value in 0.5-10 / 0-5,000 / 0-1 loads.
(b) The gather rates **0.85 / 0.75** are my numbers for "a little quicker"; `rules.json` `gatherRate`. (c) The mage aims at the **nearest**
group, not the **densest** one you named on 2026-10-14: nearest was the small, deterministic step and fixes the two-groups case; the
remaining gap is a lone enemy standing in front of a group behind it (the mage then casts nothing until something moves). Write "densest
cluster" in the inbox if you want the full rule; otherwise it stays as built.

**Rough edges.** **BUG-0790** (S3): with 40 workers on a gold mine that is open on one side only, one worker can stand 3-4 seconds just
out of reach of the mine next to a free spot (the quicker trips crowd the face harder; the old rates never did it in the same test). You
won't see it at normal worker counts (5-20 on two mines); fixed at the next sim clean-up (M5-H3, two sessions away). **BUG-0791** (S4): in
one very crowded test scene the AI's thinking takes about 1 ms more per second than before, all inside its budget; same clean-up. The
replays you record from now on (see the next entry) stop playing whenever a game number changes, this change included: that is by design.

**How to change it.** Edit `game/data/common/rules.json` (`ai.defendRatio` / `defendMinValue` / `recallHallHp`, `gatherRate`), or write it in
the inbox ("defend ratio 2", "gold 1.0 a second", "densest cluster") and the data track does it.

### Every match you play is recorded, and Main menu → Load Game lets you watch it back (view track, M6-V9, 2026-10-16)

**What was built.** Every match you start from the menu (or with `--skirmish`) is recorded while you play. When it ends (the Victory /
Defeat / Draw banner), when you quit to the menu, or when you close the window mid-match, the recording is written to the game's user
folder (`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\RtsGame\replays\`, named by date, time and seed, for example `20261016-203605-seed7.replay`). The
**newest 20** are kept; older ones are deleted. The main menu has a new **Load Game** button (between Skirmish and Settings): it lists your
recordings newest first with the **date, seed, players** (each side's faction and "You", "Human" or the AI's difficulty) and **length**
(m:ss), and has **Watch**, **Delete** and **Back**. **Watch** replays the match from the start: free camera, the minimap, Esc pauses, you can
select units to read their panel, but **no order of any kind is accepted** (the command card is greyed; right clicks and hotkeys do
nothing). It ends with a "Replay ended" banner (or the match's own Victory / Defeat if it ended on the recording's last moment) with Stats
and Main menu. You see the match through **your own side's fog**, as you played it. `--replay <path>` on the command line plays a file directly.

**What you will see.** Play a short skirmish, quit to the menu, press Load Game: one row, something like
"2026-10-16 22:53 | 7 | Malazan Empire (You), The Whirlwind (Normal) | 0:04". Watch it: your units repeat exactly what they did. Until
save / load exists (it needs the rules side's save format first), Load Game shows replays only.

**Two things to know.** (1) **A replay stops playing when the game's numbers change.** Each file remembers the data it was recorded with; after
any balance change (every data task, and rules changes like this session's gather rates) older files are refused with "This replay can't be
played: it was recorded with different game data, or the file is damaged." That is deliberate for now (a silent wrong replay would be
worse); the files stay listed so you can Delete them. (2) A file that was damaged or edited stops with "Replay out of sync" at the first
moment it disagrees.

**New text in the game**, all in `game/data/common/ui.json` (`menu.load`, `load.*`): "Load Game"; the columns "Date", "Seed", "Players",
"Length"; the buttons "Watch", "Delete", "Back"; "No replays yet. Every match you play is recorded here."; "{0} unreadable replay file(s)
skipped"; "This replay can't be played: it was recorded with different game data, or the file is damaged."; "Replay out of sync";
"Replay ended". Change any of them in that file.

**Producer decisions.** The 20-file cap (a code constant, `ReplayStore.MaxReplays`; a one-hour match is a few MB; write "keep 50 replays" in
the inbox to change it). The file name uses your PC's clock (view side only; nothing of the clock reaches the rules). Load Game lists
replays until the save format lands, then both.

**Rough edges (BUG-0830, S4, fixed at the next view clean-up, M6-VH3, two sessions away).** An unreadable file in the folder counts toward the
20 and can't be deleted from the screen; if the PC's clock jumps back (daylight saving, a copied folder) a file with a later-dated name can
push out the one you just saved; nothing on screen says "Replay" while one plays; the list opens slowly (1-2 s) when the folder holds 20
hour-long matches. None of this loses a recording you can see in the list.

### You can now play against two or three AIs at once: the skirmish setup takes 2-4 players, each AI with its own faction, difficulty and colour (view track, M6-V5, 2026-10-16)

**What was built.** The skirmish screen has two new buttons, **"Add player"** and **"Remove player"**. The setup opens with
two slots as before (you and one AI); Add player shows a third and a fourth row, each an AI with its own faction list,
colour list and difficulty list (Easy / Normal / Hard, Normal by default). You are always slot 1. Colours stay unique: each
list greys out the colours the other players hold, and if you pick a taken one the game moves you to the first free colour.
A removed slot remembers its picks if you add it back. Start builds a base for every player on its own start location (the
map generator already made 3 or 4 mirrored start spots, each with two gold mines and a forest in reach), so a 4-player map has
four bases a quarter turn apart.

**What you'll see.** Skirmish → Add player twice → pick, say, Whirlwind Hard, Malazan Easy, Whirlwind Normal → Start: four
Town Halls with five workers each, four colours on the minimap and on the units. It is a free-for-all: the AIs fight each
other as much as you. The banner reads **Victory** only when you are the last side standing; **Defeat** the moment your side is
out, even while the other AIs are still fighting, with **Continue watching** to see who wins; **Draw** if the last sides fall
together. The stats table lists every seat with its time of defeat. From the command line: `--players 4 --ai 3 hard` (the
old `--ai hard` still means slot 2, so nothing existing changed).

**Checks.** QA ran 1,168 flag combinations and 516 setup combinations, two 3,000-step fuzzes of the colour rule, 29 real starts
on three map sizes (every hall on its start spot, more than 20 m apart, each seeing a gold mine), a 4-player match run twice to
the same fingerprint at every checkpoint, and the three match-over paths above. No bugs found. The two test scenes that still
read your real `settings.cfg` were moved onto their own throw-away files (BUG-0770 closed; your file's checksum was unchanged
over the whole run with a rebound key in it).

**Rough edges.** **No teams yet**: the "team" column from the design needs a small sim change first (Requests 38; the AI would
also need to know who its allies are), so every match is free-for-all. The dev-only `--units` army flag only arms players 1 and
2 (3 and 4 get a base and no army; documented). One cosmetic warning in the log says "Ignoring --colour: slot 2 ..." even when
slot 2 never asked for a colour (the next view clean-up, M6-VH3).

**How to change it.** The button labels are `game/data/common/ui.json` (`setup.add_slot` "Add player", `setup.remove_slot`
"Remove player"). The default difficulty for new AI slots is Normal (an inbox line changes it). If you want the slot cap higher
than 4, that is the map generator's start-location limit (sim); say so in the inbox.

### When a side is knocked out its leftover buildings fall with it, a soldier pinned against a cliff by idle friends slides free, and the AI stops stacking sandstorms (sim track, M5-H2 clean-up, 2026-10-16)

**What was built (a clean-up: no new feature, no number changed, the recorded matches unmoved).**
1. **The collapse.** Under your win rule a side is out when it has no unit left and nothing that can train one, but its houses,
   towers, Forge and half-built sites used to stand on and keep working: its tower kept shooting and scoring kills, its research
   finished. Now, on the tick a side is out, every building it still has crumbles like a razed one: rubble on the ground, the
   ground reopens, anything queued in it is gone.
2. **Rings shared by two sides.** Two players attacking one building (a 3-4 player match later) used to read each other's
   standing spots as taken; each side now has its own ring, and a spot is judged by who is actually standing on it. A sealed
   pocket's unreachable spots are no longer tried first (attack-moving into a walled House: 9 give-ups → 0).
3. **The pinned Sapper.** The M4 playable scene's Sapper stood still through eight right-clicks because the army had been
   pulled back on top of it against a cliff: the sidestep round idle friends cancelled its way along the wall. A unit in that
   spot now slides on past them (replayed in a bare sim: 0.07 m in 8 orders before, 55 m after).
4. **The AI's spells.** Three Priests no longer drop three sandstorms on one spot in one think (one storm, the others keep their
   casts; a storm that never landed is retried as before), and the AI's thinking no longer slows down with every live storm (8
   storms: 1.1 ms → 0.27 ms per think). A site no worker can reach is given up on after three tries instead of draining the
   economy forever.

**What you'll see.** Win a skirmish against the AI: the moment its last soldier and its last unit-making hall are gone, its houses,
towers and sites all turn to rubble at once instead of standing as a ghost base you'd have to hunt down, and no tower keeps
shooting your army after the banner. The end-screen counts: a collapse is **neither a kill for you nor a loss for the AI** (see the
decision). Pathing: an army parked on top of a unit against a cliff no longer freezes that unit. Spells: an AI with several
Priests spends its storms on different clumps rather than one.

**Producer decision (owner may revisit).** A collapsed building counts as neither a kill nor a loss in the post-match stats: the
stats count what the enemy destroyed, and a collapse is the consequence of a defeat already decided. The alternative, crediting
them to the winner, would pad kill counts by a whole base in every win. One inbox line changes it ("count collapses as kills").
Two smaller closures: BUG-0651 (one unit of 1,000 gave up a reachable building at twice the supported crowd) **no longer
reproduces** on today's chase code and is closed with its test kept as a guard; a defense radius covering the whole map is
documented as a legal "turtle" play style, not a bug.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0702 item 1 (a mage with two enemy groups either side casts at neither; goes with the proportional defense
task), BUG-0704 items 2-3 (wording and two test rows weaker than their names; next sim clean-up), BUG-0144 and BUG-0113 item 2
not reached again, **BUG-0764 (new, S3): 17-20 speed benchmarks fail on this PC on every branch alike, so they can't catch a
regression until re-baselined** (a fresh-boot check from you is wanted, see Waiting on you), and `CLAUDE.md` still says
"Current milestone: M1" (one line; the next sim session fixes it unless you prefer to). Around a small House the last two or
three attackers still jam at the far corners (17-18 of 20): pathing slice 2. The memory bound of the biggest test map moved up
by 168 KB (one ring layer per player plus the fog's storm mask), itemised.

### The keybinds file refuses look-alike combos, test scenes stop sharing one settings file, and the M4 playable scene runs on a fixed clock (view track, M6-VH2 clean-up, 2026-10-16)

**What was built (a clean-up: nothing new on screen).** A hand-edited `settings.cfg` key such as "Meta+K", "Cmd+K" or "Kp+K" used
to be read silently as plain K; it is now one reported problem and the default key, and a key value that can't survive a save
is refused up front (1.1 million codes checked, 261 real keys, none lost). The Settings screen greys out VSync and shows the real
state when a developer flag forces it, and never writes that flag into your file. The benchmark now frames the whole army before
boxing it (seed 6's column used to be half off screen). The "Last seen" amount on a clicked mine is exact at 2x speed. The two
settings test scenes each use their own folder, so two test runs at once can't trip each other; and a start location by the
map's west or north edge no longer puts a hall across the map (hand-built maps only; the menu's maps were never affected). The
M4 playable test scene now advances the clock by a fixed 1/60 s per frame, so every click lands on the same tick however busy
the PC is: the two "failed once under load" cases (BUG-0745) are closed, together with the sim's fix above.

**What you'll see.** Nothing different in play. If you ever edit `settings.cfg` by hand and mistype a key, the game tells you
which one and uses the default.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0770 (S4): two test scenes still read your real `settings.cfg`, so a rebind on your desk could fail them
(the game itself is unaffected; next view clean-up). BUG-0744 item 3: one bad hand-edited key can reset a whole row of grid keys
(documented as the chosen behaviour). A side effect worth knowing: the seed-6 benchmark runs at a wider zoom now, so its frame
times aren't comparable with earlier runs.

### Your soldiers now surround a building instead of queueing behind each other: 17-20 of 20 strike within ten seconds, where 9-11 did before (sim track, M5-P1 "pathing slice 1", 2026-10-15)

**What was built.** Your playtest note 5. Every building now has a ring of standing spots round its walls (two per wall cell on each
side, one off each corner: 20 round a House, 28 round a hall, 36 round a Town Hall). A melee soldier sent at a building takes the
nearest spot nobody of yours holds and walks there; if every spot is taken it waits just behind and grabs the first one a death or a
retreat frees. Nobody gives a building up any more because it is "stuck behind friends": an order on a reachable building keeps on
in every mode (your right-click, attack-move, the AI's waves). Archers and crossbowmen are unchanged (they stop at range anyway).

**What you'll see.** Select 20 Heavy Infantry, right-click an enemy hall: they spread round three or four sides and almost all of
them swing within ten seconds (measured: House 17-18 of 20, hall 20 of 20, Town Hall 19-20 of 20; before, 9-11 of 20 and the rest
shuffled behind). Attack-move an army past a lone House: it is razed with nobody walking off. Combined with the data track's faster
building damage (next entry), a 20-man line now razes a House in well under 20 s instead of over a minute.

**Producer decision (owner may revisit).** The spots a soldier "holds" steer the next step but are left out of the match fingerprint
(the hash that proves two runs are identical), because putting them in would change every recorded checkpoint for no change in play.
The cost: when save / load arrives (M6), the save must store those spots too, and a later test must compare them directly. Recorded
in the technical doc; the alternative (hash them now) is a one-session change if you prefer belt and braces.

**Rough edges.** Round a small House the last two or three attackers can still jam at the far corners (17-18 of 20, not 20); routing
round your own standing archers is the next pathing slice. Two small nits (BUG-0732: a sealed pocket's unreachable spots are tried first
in a test-only layout; with three or more players a rival's spots count as taken) go to the next sim clean-up. **The faction pages'
siege-vs-infantry times moved with this rule and are re-printed by the data track as this lands** (BUG-0734; no change in play).

**How to change it.** An inbox line: "two spots per cell is too tight" (one constant), "hash the spots now" (one session), or a
different fill order ("far sides first").

### Click a gold mine or a tree to see what is left, and every hotkey is rebindable from Settings → Keybinds (view track, M6-V8, 2026-10-16)

**What was built.** Your playtest note 8: a left click on a mine or a tree selects it alone (your units are deselected, no order is
sent) and the selection panel shows its name and "2500 Gold left" / "40 Wood left", live while any of your units or buildings can see
it. For a node in explored but unwatched ground it shows "Last seen: 2498 Gold left", the amount from the last time you saw it; a node

grid keys). Click a key, press the new one; a key another command uses is refused with a line saying which; "Default keys" puts them
back. Saved in `settings.cfg` under `[keys]`; the command card's hints follow your keys. Esc, Shift / Ctrl / Alt, the arrow keys, F10
and F12 stay fixed; mouse buttons and the camera keys aren't rebindable yet.

**What you'll see.** Start a skirmish, click the gold mine by your hall: "Gold Mine / 2500 Gold left", counting down as your workers
mine it. Walk every unit away and watch the fog dim it: "Last seen: ...". Open Settings → Keybinds, click Attack-move, press K: A does
nothing now, K + click attack-moves; try to bind Stop to K and the line says K is already Attack-move.

one scripted playtest scene (the Sapper's Cusser step) failed once while three test suites shared the PC and passed alone; the sim

### The win condition is yours now: a side is out when it has no units left and nothing that can train one; houses, camps, the Forge and towers don't have to be hunted down (sim track, M5-4e, 2026-10-14)

**What was built.** Your playtest note 9, as the rule. A player is out the moment it has had a building, has **no unit alive** and
**no finished building that trains units** (the Town Hall or any of the five unit halls; for the Whirlwind that includes the Holy
Camp, Raider Camp and Archer Camp). Houses, the drop-off camp (Depot / Supply Cache), the Forge, towers and half-built sites keep
nobody in. A summoned unit counts while it lives. A side that never had a building still can't lose (the test sandboxes). The
end-screen, the stats and the AI going quiet all key off the same flag, so nothing else changed.

**What you'll see.** Raze the enemy's Town Hall and every hall while one of their workers is still alive: no Victory yet; kill the
worker (or it dies trying to rebuild): Victory on that tick. Lose your own hall but keep workers and money: you can still rebuild
and are not out. Win while the loser's houses and towers still stand: the banner shows; the houses stay for now (see the decision
below). The dev console line now reads "Match over: player 1 is defeated".

**Caveat you already know.** As in Age of Empires, a last hidden worker keeps a side alive; the AI's waves target buildings, so an
AI-vs-AI match can now stall on one until the sim's M5-4d adds "hunt the last units". If that annoys you in play, an inbox line "a
side with no hall for 3 minutes is out" is a 20-line rule.

**Producer decision (owner may revisit).** The question the new rule opened: what do a loser's remaining buildings do? Today they
keep acting (its towers shoot and score kills, its Forge finishes research), which in a 3-4 player match would let a player who is
already out knock someone else out. I chose: **when a player is out, its remaining buildings collapse on that tick**, like razed
ones, nobody credited the kill (recorded in the design doc; built at the sim's next clean-up session, BUG-0703). The alternatives
were "they stand as inert ruins" (a special state every system must know) or "they fight on until razed" (the knock-out problem).
To change it: an inbox line "the loser's buildings stay as ruins" or "they keep fighting".

**Rough edges.** BUG-0703 (S3, above, next sim clean-up); BUG-0704 (S4, test wording and two weaker test rows, same session). Two
bugs QA found in the fix round are closed: 14 old test scenes placed a House before any unit and would silently have been "out"
(BUG-0705 / 0706; they now keep a worker alive).

### Edge panning works beside a second monitor, control groups can hold a building, and the match-over screens were restaged for the new win rule (view track, M6-V7, 2026-10-14)

**What was built.** Note 1: the game saw no cursor at the edge because the mouse had left the window onto your second monitor. Now,
**while a match runs** (unpaused, window focused) **the cursor stays inside the window**, so every edge pans; the pause menu, the
match-over banner, the settings screen, the main menu and Alt-Tab all free it. A Settings row **"Confine cursor to window"** (On by
default) turns it off. The very last pixel column / row counts as the edge, so a cursor pinned at the border pans. Note 7: Ctrl + a
digit with a **building** selected stores that building in the group (a group holds units or one building, never both); the digit
selects it again from anywhere, with its command card; a double-tap centres the camera on it; a razed building drops out of its
group. Also: the "K / L" line under the Victory banner now agrees with the stats screen (BUG-0710), and a dead piece of code is gone.

**What you'll see.** Start a skirmish, push the mouse toward the other monitor: the cursor stops at the window edge and the map
scrolls. Press Esc: the cursor is free to leave. Select your Billet, Ctrl + 1; walk the camera away; press 1: the Billet is selected
with its Train buttons; press 1 again quickly: the camera jumps to it.

**D14 feasibility verdict: feasible, worth doing, in stages.** The AI's cost today is 0.4 ms per think for eight Hard seats over 2,600
units (gate 1 ms), and every AI read goes through its fog-limited window (a test fails the build if AI code names the world directly), so
every stage below is vision-limited by construction and adds work proportional to the units it can see, not a search.
(a) **Proportional defense** (next session): below. (b) **A strategy per match** (~1 sim session for the file format, ~1 data session for
the openings): `ai.json` holds several named openings per faction (build order, army mix, attack thresholds, e.g. Malazan "legion push" /
"fast casters" / "towers and siege"; Whirlwind "early raid" (the 4:30 Raider raid the page sketched) / "horde" / "priest timing"); the AI
draws one with its seeded dice at the start (Easy always the first), so matches differ and replays still reproduce. Zero think cost.
(c) **Counter-composition** (~1 sim session + a small data table): the AI remembers which enemy unit types it has seen in the last few
minutes (each unit once, fading) and shifts its army mix toward their counters from the template table (Line counters Shock, Ranged
counters casters and light units, Shock counters Ranged, casters counter clumped Line, siege counters buildings) by a strength per
difficulty (Easy 0, Normal moderate, Hard strong). Cost: a few hundred operations per think. (d) **Attack and defence at once, not
discrete waves** (2-3 sim sessions, **after** M5's remaining criteria): squads with roles (a home guard sized by the last raid, a main
army that gets reinforcements streamed to it instead of waiting for the next wave, a harass squad of fast units sent at undefended
workers it has scouted). (a)-(c) are new M5 criteria in docs/05; (d) is queued after M5-5 so M5 doesn't balloon; you decide after
playing (a)-(c) whether (d) is worth it. What I would **not** do: a planner that searches moves ahead (think cost, and it would play
like a machine, not an opponent).

**Design: proportional defense ("partial recall by threat", M5-4f).** Today any raid (one building hit, or any enemy soldier within 48 m
of the hall) sends the **whole** army home for 20 s and aborts a wave: exactly the exploit you spotted. The new rule:
1. **Measure the threat.** Each think the AI already counts the enemy soldiers it can see within 48 m of its hall. It now also adds up
   what they are worth (their gold + wood cost). A building being hit by something it can't see (a catapult behind the fog) counts as a
   fixed minimum threat (`ai.defendMinValue`, 150 = about two line units).
2. **Size the answer.** It commits defenders worth `ai.defendRatio` × the threat (1.5: a 120-cost Horse Raider pulls at most 180 worth,
   two soldiers), never less than `defendMinValue`.
3. **Who goes, in order.** First the **home army** (units not in the wave: rallying, fresh from the halls), nearest the threat first.
   If that isn't enough, **part of the wave**: the members nearest home, as long as the wave keeps at least its start threshold (the size
   it needed to be sent at all); a wave that would drop below that comes home whole (a half-wave achieves nothing). The **whole wave**
   also comes home when the hall itself is under attack and below half hp (`ai.recallHallHp`, 0.5). New units from the halls keep
   joining the defense while the threat holds.
4. **What stays.** Workers still flee a threat within 16 m and return 20 s later; the 20-second hold after the last hit; defenders
   attack-move to the threat and go back to the rally point after.
5. **Why it isn't trickable.** A small raid costs you more than it costs the AI: it answers with 1.5× your raid's worth and keeps its
   attack going. Dancing a raider in and out re-sends nothing (the point only moves when the threat really moves). A raid it can't catch
   (kiting cavalry) holds two soldiers at home, not the army. A big raid gets the big answer it deserves. The knobs are three numbers in
   `rules.json` (`defendRatio`, `defendMinValue`, `recallHallHp`), one fingerprint update, and tests pin: a 2-unit raid against a 20-unit
   wave out → the wave continues and ≤ 3 units come home; a 15-unit raid → the wave returns; a hit with nobody seen → the minimum.
   Same rule on every difficulty for now (a per-difficulty ratio is a one-field schema change if Hard should defend tighter).

**Order of work from here** (inbox requests before roadmap items, as the rules say): this session sim M5-4e (win rule), view M6-V7
(edge-pan + building groups + BUG-0710 + the match-over scenes re-staged for the new rule), data D18 (reports). Next: sim M5-4f
(proportional defense + D15 C + the densest-cluster target), view the resource click + keybinds, data D19 (apply ×1.5, Easy casts,
building damage, gather rates, Line v Shock numbers). Then sim pathing slice 1 and 2, the Hard knobs (M5-4c slice 2), the stats counters
(Requests 39), D14 b's format, M5-4d (expansion, rebuilding, re-scouting, hunting), D14 c, the 20-minute test, your Easy / Hard play.
The Ages design task after that. Nothing of M6's view work is displaced except by one session.

**How to change any of it.** An inbox line per item: "defendRatio 2", "gather 0.9 / 0.8", "House must take 30 s", "skip the Ages design
until M6", "do pathing before the defense".

### The AI casts spells now: a Normal or Hard opponent sets fire to your clumps, blasts your buildings and calls sandstorms onto your army; Easy never casts (sim track, M5-4c slice 1, 2026-10-13)

**What was built.** The last of the AI's managers: the one that decides when and where to cast. After everything else in its
think (defense, build order, scouting, economy, production, the army), every AI unit that has a spell ready and is free (not already
casting, not walking to a cast, not the scout, not fleeing, not on its way home from a wave) may get one cast order a think, through
exactly the same door your own Q-click uses. **Where:** it looks at the enemy units it can see within the spell's reach, takes the
middle of that group, keeps only the enemies within the spell's radius of that middle, and casts there if **at least 2** of your units
are inside the blast (a number in the rules file). If the point is a little beyond the spell's range it is pulled back to the range,
so the caster never walks into your line. A spell that hurts buildings (the Sapper's Cusser) goes at the nearest enemy building it
can see when no group of your units qualifies. A spell that would hurt its own side (the Cusser again) is **never** thrown with one of
its own units in the blast, the Sapper included. It can't hear "no" from the rules, so it judges a cast by the spell's cooldown
starting: if the cast didn't happen it tries again next think, at most three times at one spot. Only Normal and Hard cast; Easy's
"doesn't use abilities" is now real (proven: 0 casts in 5 minutes beside a casting Normal twin).

**What you will see.** Skirmish vs "The Whirlwind" on Normal or Hard: when its wave with Priests meets your army, a **dust storm lands
on the thickest part of your line** (your units in it are Blinded and Slowed, as before). Vs the Malazans: a Cadre Mage **sets the
ground ablaze under two or more of your soldiers** the moment they bunch, and a Sapper **lobs the Cusser at your house or tower** when
nothing better is in reach, never into a melee its own soldiers are in. Spread your units out and the mages wait; walk a lone unit past
and nothing happens. On Easy none of this happens.

**Producer decisions.** (1) *The target rule* above (the middle of the group in reach, at least 2 enemies in the blast). The
alternative, "the densest cluster", is better when your army is in two groups (see the rough edge below) and may come later. (2)
*No friendly fire ever*, rather than "worth it when the enemy group is big": simpler and never embarrassing. (3) *Casting is judged
by the cooldown, three tries at one spot*: a code guard, not a balance number. (4) *The three remaining Hard knobs* (25 % gather bonus,
focus fire, pulling back wounded) were **deferred** to the next slice: the manager alone passed the size limit set for it, and the
builder stopped and said so, which is what the limit is for. (5) *The AI's speed test turns the storms' vision-blocking off* so it
measures the AI and not the fog (BUG-0701 below); a rule now says any such test must say so and the hidden cost gets its own row.

**Rough edges.** BUG-0701 (S3): each live storm adds about 0.03 ms to every AI think (the fog checks every unit against every storm);
fine at the handful of storms a real match has, fixed in the sim's next clean-up. BUG-0702 (S4): three targeting nits: your army split
in two groups either side of a mage gets no fire at all (the middle is empty ground); three Priests may stack three storms on one spot
in the same instant (wasteful, not wrong); a group standing exactly at the far edge of reach is never cast on. Hard plays like Normal
plus casting until the next slice lands its three knobs.

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/rules.json` → `ai.castMinTargets` (1-50; 1 = cast at any lone unit, 5 = only at real
clumps). "Cast at the densest cluster", "never two storms on one spot" or "let the Cusser hit its own side when the prize is big"
would be inbox notes.

### The match ends on screen: a Victory / Defeat / Draw banner, a stats table and "Continue watching"; the two red test scenes are fixed and `--resolution` works again (view track, M6-V4, 2026-10-13)

**What was built.** The window now watches the sim's defeat rule. The moment **you** (always the first slot) have no building left, a
**Defeat** banner pauses the match; when the enemy's last building falls, **Victory**; if the last two sides fall in the same instant,
**Draw**. One banner per match, with three buttons: **Stats**, **Continue watching** and **Main menu**. **Stats** is a table with the
match length at the top and one row per player: a colour swatch, the faction name, "You" or the AI's difficulty, then **Kills**,
**Losses**, **Gold in hand**, **Wood in hand** and **Defeated at** (the clock time the player fell, or "Standing"). **Continue
watching** hides the banner for good and lets the match run on (after a defeat your clicks do nothing, but you can watch the AI finish;
Esc is the pause menu as before, which now offers Stats too). **Main menu** ends the match. Also: the two test scenes that were red on
`main` since the last session are fixed (BUG-0674, BUG-0680), and a settings file no longer overrides a `--resolution` or
`--fullscreen` flag you pass on the command line (BUG-0681).

**What you will see.** Skirmish vs Hard, send nothing, wait: when its wave razes your last building the game freezes under a dimmed
"Defeat", three buttons in the middle. Click Stats: "Match length 6:40", your row with Kills 3 / Losses 14 and "Defeated at 6:40", the
AI's row "Standing". Back, then Continue watching: the match resumes, you can scroll around and watch. Or raze the AI's base yourself
(it has only a hall and houses early) and get "Victory" with the AI's row showing when it fell.

**Producer decisions.** (1) *Defeat shows the moment you fall, even if other sides still stand* (3-4 player matches later); the
alternative, waiting for the whole match to end, would have you watching a game you lost with no word. (2) *The banner pauses the match*
like the pause menu; the alternative, a small non-blocking message, would let the last fight run on while you read. (3) *The stats show
only what the sim counts today.* The design doc's full list (resources gathered, units trained, buildings built and lost, time to Age
II, an army-value graph) needs counters the sim doesn't keep yet; they are on the sim's list (Requests 39) and drop in as columns.
Gold and wood are what the player **holds** now, labelled "in hand" so nobody reads them as "gathered". (4) *A small piece of
stand-in code* the view used before the sim's rule existed is kept this one session because QA's tests still cover it; it is dead and
goes next view task (BUG-0710).

**Rough edges.** BUG-0710 (S4): the small "K / L" counter in the top-right corner, visible through the banner, is one tick behind the
stats table (the pause lands inside the killing tick); cosmetic, next view task. In dev runs only, a player who never built anything
can "win" when another falls; the menu's match always gives everyone a hall, so you won't see it.

**How to change it.** `game/data/common/ui.json` → `match_over`: every word ("Victory", "Defeat", "Draw", "Continue watching",
"Gold in hand" ...) and the clock format. "Don't pause on the banner", "show the banner only when the match is over" or "add a
Rematch button" would be inbox notes.
